# Business Partners

We're always looking for new partners to help us better serve our Marines and family members.

The procurement of equipment, supplies, support services, revenue-generating services, and professional services is accomplished at both the Headquarters and the MCCS field activity level. These procurements are considered non-retail or non-resale. To inquire about selling items through retail channels, such as the Marine Corps Exchange, [click here](https://www.mymcx.com/about/partnerships) to learn more.

## MCCS Contracting Office
Headquarters, U.S. Marine Corps
Business & Support Services Division (MR)
Attn: Procurement (MRB)
3044 Catlin Avenue
Quantico, VA 22134-5099

Email: hqmcnafcontracting@usmc-mccs.org

To be added to the source list and considered for future procurements, interested vendors must contact each MCCS Contracting Office. We do not use a standard source application; simply provide your company name, website address, contact information, and a short summary of products or services.

## Examples of non-resale procurement
**Equipment & Supply Items:**
- Cell Phones and Service
- Food Service Equipment
- Retail Fixtures
- IT Hardware and Software
- Recreation & Fitness Equipment

**Support Services:**
- Grounds Keeping
- Printing & Advertising
- Distribution Services
- Small Construction
- Maintenance and Repair

**Revenue-generating Services**
- Barber and Beauty Shop Services
- Vending Machines and Products
- Golf Courses
- Laundry/Dry Cleaning
- Foodservice

**Professional Services:**
- Banking, Audit, and Credit Card Processing Services
- Feasibility Studies
- Employee Development Training
- Consultant Services
- Instructors

These goods and services are purchased for our Marine Corps Exchanges, clubs, lodging facilities, recreation activities and warehouse facilities. We also contract with nationally recognized companies for fast food operations, money transfer services, and film processing, to name a few.

Our non-resale procurement professionals may also order against other NAFI and Federal Government contracts, such as those issued by the General Services Administration and Air Force Nonappropriated Fund Purchasing Office (AFNAFPO).

It is our policy that procurement using nonappropriated funds be accomplished primarily through competition in a fair, equitable, and impartial manner, and to the best advantage of the MCCS. MCCS contracting is entitled to the same tax exemptions and adheres to the same tax regulations as other Federal agencies. The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) does not apply to non-appropriated fund procurements, except when specifically required by DoD Directive, Instruction, or Component regulations.

## Contract Clauses/General Provisions Downloads
Listed below are the General Provision documents available for download. To view the document, simply click on the document title. For the current MCX Terms and Conditions and Vendor Standards Guide, visit https://www.mymcx.com/about/partnerships

# Marine For Life Cycle

(Long page, shortened here: each section's opening only. Fetch the page for the full text.)

## First Permanent Duty Station (PDS) Checklist
Congratulations and welcome aboard! You have completed your initial training and finally arrived to your new home at your first PDS. You are probably busy checking in to your new unit and exploring your new installation. You will attend the Personal Readiness Seminar (PRS) where you will discover the services available to you throughout your Marine Corps career. Just as you learned to orient a map during land navigation classes, you must also orient yourself in your new location. Work through the checklist below to ensure you start your Marine Corps career off on the right foot.

## Marine for Life Cycle Resources
- Personal Readiness Seminar
- VA Veteran Centers
- Capstone
- STARS
- Employment Preparation
- Accessing Higher Education
- Career & Technical Training
- Entrepreneurship

## Reenlistment Checklist
Congratulations Marine! As you complete your enlistment there are many options available to you. Your decision to "stay Marine" comes with a completely new set of challenges and opportunities. Re-enlistment is a good time to reevaluate your Individual Development Plan (IDP). Consider meeting with a Personal and Professional Development Advisor to discuss opportunities and programs available to you. Perhaps you'd like to pursue new educational interests or explore credentials and apprenticeships, or maybe you will be receiving a re-enlistment bonus and would like to learn more about saving and investing. You may also be preparing to PCS or transition to a "B" billet.The topics below will assist you to make sound and timely decisions regarding this transition.

## Promotion Checklist
Congratulations Marine! Promotion is an exciting time. More responsibility and more pay! It's also a great time to evaluate your Individual Development Plan. Schedule an appointment with a Personal & Professional Development Advisor (P&PD) to discuss your goals. Do you have an emergency fund? Are you planning for retirement? Your income is growing; your Personal Financial Manager (PFM) or Command Financial Specialist (CFS) can provide workshops and one on one counseling to help you reach your financial goals. While you are adjusting to your new rank, it's not too early to begin preparing for your next promotion. Keep yourself technically and tactically proficient. The links below will help you achieve success.

## Deployment Checklist
Preparation is critical to a successful deployment. In addition to preparing your gear and your Marines, you must ensure your personal affairs are in order. Your command will provide opportunities to complete pre-deployment preparations. The topics below will provide additional resources to assist in your personal deployment preparation.

## PCS Checklist
Whether this is your first PCS or your tenth, proper preparation and planning will make the process much smoother. It's never too early to begin setting aside a PCS fund to ensure those unexpected expenses don't result in financial hardship. Once you have received your orders you'll want to begin researching your new duty station and preparing your family and household goods for the move. Your new command will assign a sponsor to assist you as you settle in at your new unit.

pages.title: MCCS Connected
pages.text:
# MCCS Connected

## What is the Semper Connected Toolkit
The Semper Connected Toolkit outlined here is designed to assist spouses/family members in the creation of a community social network to connect and support spouses/family members through engagement, social events, and periodic check ins.

Contact and similar information is collected with permission from incoming spouses/family members by another spouse/family members within the unit. This information may be shared with other members of the Semper Connected team and will be used as a resource to support individual spouses/family members. The provision of contact and similar information is completely voluntary but is highly recommended; connection with and support from other spouses/family members who understand the military lifestyle is the greatest resource! Semper Connected provides a bridge to unit readiness functions and resources but is not an officially mandated program.

This Toolkit shall be managed in accordance with record schedule 1000-23, "Morale and Welfare Program Management" of SECNAV M-5210.1. A complete list and explanation of the applicable routine uses is published in the authorizing SORN available at: https://dpcld.defense.gov/Privacy/SORNsIndex/DOD-wide-SORN-Article-View/Article/570630/m01754-5/

## How do I Use the Semper Connected Toolkit?
**1. Create a Social Roster**

**Step 1:** "Make a Copy" of the [Semper Connected Contact Information Google Form](https://docs.google.com/forms/u/5/d/1LwxMr7wle3xedCk9fkQ-rDAOWX8lzxTLkOESUcCF-So/copy) and **RENAME** the copy with your unit name. **DO NOT MODIFY THIS DOCUMENT**. It has been created this way to protect privacy of information.

**Step 2:** Send the link for the new *Semper Connected Contact Information* Form via your DRC/URC, your unit facebook page, or as determined by the command.

**2. Get Connected**

Making connections is very personal. There is no "right way" to do this but some options are included below.

**PHONE CALLS:** Review ["How to connect by phone"](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JpClTmrry23x-nfkh3Jds9cevZqMH62h6idXka5GPiA/edit?usp=sharing) and begin making phone calls with the phone numbers collected from the Semper Connected Contact Information Google Form.

1. Consider sending a **text message first** letting the spouse or family member know that you will be calling to say hello
2. The [Semper Connected Phone Call Log](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1znx-4nsjggRMz6gS4Dr9cov4WVjXhwE2-PV4OSsMC5U/copy) (Google Form) is a tool available to help you take notes while reaching out to spouses and family members

**How to use the Semper Connected Phone Call Log:**

1. Make a Copy of the "Semper Connected Phone Call Log"
2. Rename the Semper Connected Phone Call Log
3. Click the Eye Icon "Preview" in the Upper Right corner to fill in the information
4. You can fill this form again with each new contact
5. View all responses with the "Responses" tab and create a spreadsheet by clicking the "Sheets" icon

**EMAILS and LETTERS:** Review the [Semper Connected Sample Welcome Letter](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mQODGvdqga5wEbKSXCz1n3yOEbOLEynX_BFb8_HA0I0/edit?usp=sharing) that can be sent via email or USPS. Feel free to edit and "make it your own"; include your personal touch or use it as is.

1. Include an invitation to the next unit or spouse/family social event
2. Enclose your contact information
3. Include the resource

**Installation Help Guides (PDF):** [29 Palms](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%2029%20Palms.pdf), [Iwakuni](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Iwakuni.pdf), [Quantico](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Quantico.pdf), [Albany](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Albany.pdf), [Barstow](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Barstow.pdf), [Beaufort](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Beaufort.pdf), [Okinawa](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Okinawa.pdf), [Camp Lejeune](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Lejeune.pdf), [Camp Pendleton](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Camp%20Pendleton.pdf), [Cherry Point](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Cherry%20Point.pdf), [Hawaii](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Hawaii.pdf), [Henderson Hall](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Henderson%20Hall.pdf), [San Diego - MCRD](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20San%20Diego%20(MCRD).pdf), [Miramar](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20San%20Diego%20(Miramar).pdf), [New River](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20New%20River.pdf), [Parris Island](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Parris%20Island.pdf), [Yuma](https://usmc-mccs.org/mccs/assets/2021%20Installation%20Help%20Guide%20-%20Yuma.pdf)

## Connect by Phone
A basic guide for making your first phone call to reach out to spouses and family members in your command/unit/office/shop.

**A few things to remember before calling:**

- Consider sending a text message first letting the spouse or family member know that you will be calling to say hello
- Be friendly, your tone sets the call
- Make your phone calls when you aren't rushed and can actively listen, with minimal interruptions.
- Some people don't like talking on the phone or may be nervous, wondering why you are calling. Do your best to put them at ease
- Our Marine Corps family is an incredible group to be part of ~ THANK YOU for helping to create meaningful Marine Corps family connections!!

**Lets get started making calls**

1. Introduce yourself (first and last name) If you have met the spouse, remind them where you met them, as they may not remember. "Hi ________!! My name is _________, we met at _____________" or "My spouse works with your spouse in the (name of unit/shop)"
2. Explain why you're calling. "My spouse works at *UNIT NAME* and I am calling to welcome you and say hello."
3. Ask if they received the welcome letter you (or unit URC/DRC) sent with the local numbers and resources and unit Facebook page and unit social Facebook page? If they aren't new (ask if they are receiving information).
4. Ask about them (if it seems appropriate):
   - Are they new to the Marine Corps?
   - How long have they been married?
   - Do they work?
   - Are they involved in their (base/unit) community?
5. Ask about their family (if it seems appropriate):
   - Do they have children?
   - What are their ages?
   - How are they settling in? Adjusting to the new community?
   - Where are they from? Do they have extended family in the area to help?
6. Let them know about upcoming events, LINKS (Lifestyle, Insights, Networking, Knowledge and Skills ) classes, the Facebook page, spouse support groups. (This information can be obtained through your Unit URC/DRC (Unit Readiness Coordinator/Deployment Readiness Coordinator) and Unit, Personal and Family Readiness Program.
7. Let them know you will/might call or text again, if they would like you to.
8. If they do not want you to call them, let them know that's okay. Ask if they'd rather receive emails or texts. Make a note on the roster.
9. Let them know you enjoyed talking to them and look forward to talking to them again/ meeting them in the future.

**Keep a Semper Connected Phone Call Log:**

- Write the date you called
- Notes about the individual and his/her family (this information helps connect individual to others with similar interests, children's ages, hobbies, careers, etc)
- Items that need follow-up. (Connections to URC/DRC, resources available, chaplain support, etc.)

## Connect in Writing
Sending a personal letter, greeting card, or email is a wonderful way to welcome an individual or encourage a large group to connect. Your personal touch, including a bit about your USMC spouse experience, provides a familiar language that you both understand and speak together. Your USMC journey is something you have in common.

**Tips and Tricks**

- To ease the burden of letter writing, consider making photo copies of a typed personal letter and writing a brief message at the bottom saying "Hello!" with your signature. Include an invitation to a coffee, wine tasting, hike, or park meetup
- Include your personal business card with your contact information. If you do not have a business card, include your personal contact information in your signature line.
- Consider including your region specific Marine and Family Programs Resource Guide (Installation Help Guides, listed above)
- Ask the URC/DRC to share your "Welcome Letter" in one of their newsletters and advertise your Social group and/or Social roster
- Let your personality show through in your writing ~ a more relaxed tone could be more welcoming and put your recipient at ease and help encourage them to join
- Consider putting a note at the bottom of your email encouraging recipients to send it along to new spouses and family members
  - Language to consider "Feel free to forward this along to anyone that you might like to join our group, ALL are Welcome!" (if this language applies)
- If overseas:
  - Ask if you can include the letter in the welcome package provided by the spouse's sponsor.
  - Before you leave, purchase a bunch of cards of all types (Birthday, Thank you, Thinking About You, Congratulations) at a Dollar Store ~ there is nothing quite like receiving mail overseas!
- Letters can be left on the recipient's front step, as an alternative to postal mail

## Social Media Connections
Social media can be a great space for making personal connections. Though nothing can replace face-to-face interactions, social media can be used as a tool to connect groups, share useful information, and offer positive reassurance. Social media is also an excellent way for military spouses and families to maintain social networks as it provides a space to check in on and connect with familiar faces and places, even when we can't be physically present due to our ever-evolving military lifestyle.

Semper Connected and Marine and Family Programs have created a guidebook on "How To" set up social media pages for your military spouse and family groups. This guidebook also includes recommendations regarding content and security so that you can promote meaningful personal connections, while simultaneously maintaining the safety and security of our service members and their families.

## Best Practices
Now you've created a roster, let's make connections! Your time, budget and location will determine what works best for your group and the following are some tested and true ways to build on the initial contact. When you discover a new way to connect, share your success with us!

## Ask An Expert
This section connects you to base specific resources and our support team.

**Connect to Resources**

**In Crisis?** [Visit Military OneSource](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/)

Installation Help Guides (PDFs) for every Marine Corps installation (see list above).

## Frequently Asked Questions
**1. What is Semper Connected and how was it formed?**
During the COVID-19 pandemic, a group of spouses felt there was an even greater need for Marine Corps spouses and family members to connect. With much research, effort and an exceptional partnership with Marine and Family programs, the Semper Connected toolkit was created. Semper Connected is not an official Marine Corps program.

**2. Who can use the Semper Connected toolkit?**
The Semper Connected toolkit is available for spouses, service members or family who would like to make social connections. It can be used to start social groups within units and provides a platform to help collect contact information.

**3. How can I use the Semper Connected toolkit?**
You can use the toolkit to communicate with other spouses and family members by creating a social roster. Connections are made via emails, texts, phone calls, and welcome letters. Some ideas for creating social rosters include supper clubs, creating sports teams (kickball, softball, basketball, etc), book clubs, running clubs, playdates at the park, monthly dinners at the barracks and SO MUCH MORE!!! Additionally, the [Best Practices](https://docs.google.com/document/u/3/d/1rPpvW2UwvLTq_piB5jWTkOD64XPMb7M50vE8suJHIZI/edit) button provides creative ideas to help create social connections. Check out the training video.

**4. Is there training available for the Semper Connected Toolkit?**
Yes, a short, 10-minute training video is available. Additional assistance is available through the "Ask an Expert" email at hqmc.upfrp@usmc.mil or semperconnected@gmail.com. (Questions will be answered M-F 8:00-4:30 EST.)

**5. Is there a social media Semper Connected page?**
We've got you covered - join our [Facebook page](http://www.facebook.com/groups/semperconnected/) and stay updated on Semper Connected new developments.

**6. How can I invite spouses and family members in my unit to connect?**
The link to the Contact Information Google form can be shared several ways including posting it on your unit social media pages, hanging a flyer in the unit with the link to sign up specific unit or group, or whatever other creative ways you have to share information in your unit! The link to the Contact Information Google Form can be found under the [Get Semper Connected button](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/connected/). Make sure to follow the instructions so that you create a Contact List for your specific unit.

**7. What is the role of the Uniformed Readiness Coordinator (URC) or Deployment Readiness Coordinator (DRC) and Semper Connected?**
The URC/DRC can help spouses and family members get connected to resources. If a spouse or family member shares with another spouse that they could use support in a specific area (new baby, relationship management, child development, financial support, education, employment, etc) the spouse can provide a bridge to the URC or DRC in the unit. Additionally, they can help spread the word about official and non-official events and trainings that are being held for families in the unit.

**8. If I call a spouse or family member and they express that they could use some resources for an issue that they are having at home, what should I do?**
The URC/DRC can help spouses and family members get connected to resources. If a spouse or family member shares that they could use support in a specific area (new baby, relationship management, child development, financial support, education, employment, etc) the spouse can serve as a bridge to the URC or DRC in the unit or they can check out Help Guides at [USMC-MCCS/help](http://usmc-mccs.org/help). By providing the phone number for the URC or DRC, and then following up later, spouses can make sure the issue was addressed.

**9. What happens if I am talking to someone and they express concern about the safety of themselves or someone else in the home?**
**In the event of an active emergency, spouses should call 911 for assistance**. Support can also be provided through the Military Crisis Line at 800-273-8255 (24/7). Additional installation resources for situations such as abuse, alcohol, assault, grief, and many more are provided on the [Ask the Expert](https://usmc-mccs.org/connected/) button, at the Connect to Resources link of the Semper Connected website.

**10. How is my personal information stored and safeguarded?**
Contact and similar information is collected with permission from incoming spouses/family members within the unit. This information may be shared with other members of the Semper Connected team and will be used as a resource to support individual spouses/family members. The provision of contact and similar information is completely voluntary but is highly recommended; connection with, and support from other spouses/family members who understand the military lifestyle is the greatest resource! Personal information is collected and maintained in accordance with The Privacy Act of 1974; 10 U.S.C. 5013; Secretary of the Navy; 10 U.S.C. 5041, Headquarters, Marine Corps: function; composition; Marine Corps Order (MCO) 1754.6C, Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB); E.O. 9397 (SSN), as amended; and SORN M01754-5.

**11. If I want to be removed from Semper Connected, how do I request my removal?**
To unsubscribe, send an email to the Semper Connected spouse coordinator and include the word "Unsubscribe" in the Subject line.

Contact: Semper Connected - Ask an Expert
Email: hqmc.upfrp@usmc.mil
Email: semperconnected@gmail.com

pages.text:
# Iron Mike's

Situated within the Pacific Views Event Center (PVEC), the venue boasts breathtaking vistas of the Pacific Ocean, complete with expansive patios and a picturesque pavilion. Iron Mike's provides a welcoming lounge where you can unwind and connect with fellow service members and guests. Experience a vibrant atmosphere where friendship flourishes and family memories are made, all within our esteemed military community.

Available for private and special events, parties, and unit functions; all inquiries are welcome.

We're excited to share an important update that enhances how we serve you and elevates your overall event experience at PVEC.

As part of our commitment to greater flexibility, convenience, and customer-focused service, we are introducing a new business model that expands both our venue and catering offerings. This new approach allows us to better meet a wide range of event styles, preferences, and budgets.

PVEC has begun implementing a new catering initiative in partnership with MCCS-authorized caterers. Through this model, we will offer both venue space and indirect catering services, giving you access to a selection of trusted vendors. These approved caterers can support everything from casual gatherings to formal events, including a variety of menu options and bar services.

One of the most exciting aspects of this change is the flexibility it provides. Clients will now be able to:

• Customize catering options directly with approved vendors
• Enjoy greater control over their event budget
• Rent venue space by the hour, tailored to their specific needs

Additionally, we are removing the food and beverage minimum requirement, making it easier to plan events that align with your vision without unnecessary constraints.

At this time, we are able to assist with reserving your event date, time, and venue space. Once the catering contracts are fully finalized, food and bar services will be coordinated directly with our MCCS-approved vendors, ensuring a streamlined and personalized planning process.

We look forward to bringing you this enhanced level of service and are confident it will provide a more dynamic and enjoyable event planning experience.

We will follow up with you as soon as all options are fully available.

Thank you for your continued support!

pages.text:
# Del Mar Beach & Marina

## Alerts
**BEACH CABANAS** - Due to recent storm surges, beach cabanas are not available.

**MCO 5530.13** - To comply with the provisions of MCO 5530.13, PMO Gate Sentries will be checking all visitors requesting access to base ensuring they are in possession of a REAL ID compliant ID.

## Cottages
Spacious beachfront and marina view cottages located on the pristine Pacific Coast. Each cottage provides a private bedroom, kitchenette, dining area, living room area, flat-screen TVs, and a furnished patio with a BBQ grill. Limited pet-friendly cottages available (additional fees apply).

**Amenities**
- Beach Access (6am-10pm daily)
- Laundry Facility
- Complimentary Wi-Fi
- Guest Services Staff (6:30am-10pm daily)
- Kitchen: refrigerator, microwave, stove, pots & pans, coffee maker, table for four
- Bedrooms: queen beds, full closets
- Living Rooms & Patios: couch, flat screen tv, patio, patio chairs, BBQ grills, fire pits

## Campground
Del Mar Beach & Marina is the perfect location for Southern California camping. Choose from 116 full hook-up campsites, and enjoy a fun, clean, and secure environment all the while enjoying quality time with family and friends on the beach.

## Cottage Policies
**Changes to Reservation Lead Time Starting November 3, 2025**
Reservations will be made up to 12 months in advance, including the current month. (ex: November 1, 2025 - November 30, 2026)

**Booking Capacity**
Active Duty, Reservists, Retirees, Eligible Veterans, and DoD employees may book up to three (3) reservations in one stay. Three RV/campsites, three cottages (only one two-bedroom cottage authorized per stay), or a combination totaling three reservations. Only one accommodation can be booked during the 4th of July holiday block at Del Mar Beach.

Former military with patronage expansion privileges which consists of all service-connected disabled veterans, Medal of Honor & Purple Heart recipients, former prisoners of war, & individuals approved and designated as the primary family caregivers of eligible veterans under the Department of Veterans Affairs Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers are only authorized to book ONE reservation at a time.

Former military with patronage expansion privileges are unable to sponsor additional guests who are not dependents onto the installation unless said guests possess a valid form of military ID. For further clarification and details regarding the vetting process, please contact the Visitors Center at (760) 763-8435.

Base Policy: Former military with patronage expansion privileges must register with the Visitors Center and receive approval prior to gaining access to the installation. This process can be a few days via the Visitors Center.

**Check-in Times**
- RVs: 1pm
- Cottages: 4pm

## Cancellations
You may cancel your reservation up to 31 days prior to arrival at no penalty.

- Cancellations made to reservations less than 31 days prior to arrival will result in the loss of the deposit of one night's stay.
- Modifications will be accepted up to 15 days prior at no penalty. If you request to modify your reservation within 14 days of your scheduled arrival date, you will lose your deposit of one night's stay.
- Patrons traveling on official government orders (TAD/PCS) may cancel or modify at no penalty – proof of orders must be received prior to cancellation.

Now accepting cancellations and modification requests to existing reservations via email at: delmarbeach@usmc-mccs.org. A guest services agent will contact you within 48 hours.

## Payment
A deposit of one night's rent is due at the time of booking. The remaining balance is due in full, 14 days prior to arrival and will be automatically charged to the credit card on file. If payment is unsuccessful, your reservation will be canceled.

## Length of Stay

- Summer (Apr – Oct): Patrons may book an initial reservation for maximum of 15 nights and may book additional nights if availability permits at check-in, not to exceed 30 nights.
- Winter (Nov – Mar): Patrons may book an initial reservation for a maximum of 30 nights and may book additional nights if availability permits at check-in; patrons authorized to lodge the entire winter season (Nov 1 - Mar 31).

**Cottages/Villas**
Year-Round: Patrons may book an initial reservation for maximum of 7 nights. Patrons may extend additional nights if availability permits at check-in, not to exceed 14 nights. Advanced reservations cannot be booked consecutively to exceed the maximum number of nights per reservation.

# San Onofre Beach

Currently, there are no scheduled activities planned for the near future. See all [upcoming events](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/calendar-of-events).

**Cottages**
The San Onofre Beach Cottages is every laid-back beachgoer's ultimate getaway; patrons can enjoy quaint and quiet lodging.

**Campground**
Located at the north end of Camp Pendleton, the San Onofre Beach Campgrounds are one of three areas aboard the base that patrons can utilize year-round.

## Cottages
**Changes to Reservation Lead Time Starting November 3, 2025**
Reservations will be made up to 12 months in advance, including the current month.
(ex: November 1, 2025 – November 30, 2026)

Active Duty, Reservists, Retirees, Eligible Veterans, and DoD employees may book up to three (3) reservations in one stay. Three RV/campsites, three cottages (only one cottage authorized and San Onofre Beach), or a combination totaling three reservations. *Only one accommodation can be booked during the 4th of July holiday block at Del Mar Beach.*

Former military with patronage expansion privileges which consists of all service-connected disabled veterans, Medal of Honor & Purple Heart recipients, former prisoners of war, & individuals approved and designated as the primary family caregivers of eligible veterans under the Department of Veterans Affairs Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers are only authorized to book ONE reservation at a time. Please note, former military with patronage expansion privileges are unable to sponsor additional guests who are not dependents onto the installation unless said guests possess a valid form of military ID. For further clarification and details regarding the vetting process, please feel free to contact the Visitors Center at (760) 763-8435 or by [clicking here](https://www.pendleton.marines.mil/Main-Menu/Base-Access/Select-Veterans-Access/).

Base Policy: Former military with patronage expansion privileges must register with the Visitors Center and receive approval prior to gaining access to the installation. This process can be a few days via the Visitors Center. Without this verification, access through any security checkpoints might be denied.

# Lake O'Neill

Lake O'Neill recreational park offers fishing, hiking, rowboats, horseshoe pits, RV and tent camping, cabanas, playgrounds (includes ADA playground), basketball, softball, ADA miniature golf, and a peninsula for group activities.

## Fishing
- Permitted year-round. The lake is stocked and bait is sold at the Lake O'Neill recreation office, BLDG 26080.
- California State License and Camp Pendleton Base permit are required; both available at Pacific Plaza Exchange.

## Recreation Area
- A variety of recreational equipment is available for rent: row & paddle boats, volleyball, basketball, and baseball equipment, horseshoes, and more!
- Boats are available for rent April - October, Friday - Sunday.

## Peninsula
- For large group activities including promotions, retirements, and wedding receptions.
- Picnic cabanas, BBQ grills, electrical power, and athletic facilities are available.

## Campground
- Campsites offer water, electricity, sewer hookups, and tent camping.
- ADA-friendly sites are available.

## Camping Reservation Lead Time
**Changes to Reservation Lead Time Starting November 3, 2025**
Reservations will be made up to 12 months in advance, including the current month.

Active Duty, Reservists, Retirees, Eligible Veterans, and DoD employees may book up to three (3) reservations in one stay. Guest sites fees apply.

Please note, former military with patronage expansion privileges are unable to sponsor additional guests who are not dependents onto the installation unless said guests possess a valid form of military ID. For further clarification and details regarding the vetting process, please feel free to contact the Visitors Center at (760) 763-8435 or by [clicking here](https://www.pendleton.marines.mil/Staff/Principal-Staff/Security-and-Emergency-Services/Base-Access/#tab#visitor-center).

## Miniature Golf Rules and Regulations
- Patrons of all ages may go into the miniature golf area. However, any patron under the age of 12 is recommended to have parental supervision.
- Patrons aged 4 and older will be charged at the same rate as any other patron.
- Climbing on rocks and plants is not permitted.
- Driving golf balls or any other dangerous behavior will result in removal from the golf course, without a refund of fees.

## Cabana Regulations
- Active duty military unit family days have priority over non-military unit functions (i.e. key wives, boy scouts, YMCA, church groups, etc.).
- All military units are required to complete a Military Cabana Request form.

## Payments
A deposit of one night's rent is due at the time of booking. The remaining balance is due in full, 14 days prior to arrival and will be automatically charged to the credit card on file. If payment is unsuccessful, your reservation will be canceled.

pages.title: Child Development Centers
pages.text:
# Child Development Centers

We foster physical, cognitive, social, and emotional development in a safe and nurturing environment for children ages 6 weeks to 5 years.

## Getting Started Is Easy
Offering guidance and resources to simplify child care registration.

### How to Get Started

Families seeking child care are required to submit their requests through [Military Child Care](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome) (MCC).

To initiate a request, families must first create an account with MilitaryChildCare.com, log in, and complete their household profile using the steps outlined in the link below.

[Create an Account](https://www.mcccentral.com/training-center/components/family-user-account-and-household-profile#801)

### Forms

The following forms are required for registering for child care.

Filling out pdf forms while using a government computer can be limited and recommend using a personal computer.

Please contact your local CDC with any questions, difficulties, or concerns you may have.

* [Child and Youth Programs Health Assessment](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media?do=download&id=3490d39d-a951-4831-a364-dc3078f2b734&v=1)
* [Child and Youth Programs Registration Form](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media?do=download&id=a20869e0-cd7e-423a-93d3-ef5fbbe59786&v=1)
* [CYP Non-Medicated Topical Products Form](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media?do=download&id=3a6d9279-f207-4d0e-9400-1245c683da9e&v=1)
* [Application for Department of Defense Childcare Fees](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media?do=download&id=20990cf2-e066-429b-b1f1-8de9b1782731&v=1)

Download the files and save them to a folder on your MAC or Windows computer. Make sure to open the file from the new location. If you do not have Adobe Acrobat Reader, please visit [Adobe](https://get.adobe.com/reader/) to download it for free.

### Request a Tour

Touring one of the Child Development Centers (CDCs) through Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) can be an enlightening and heartwarming experience. Our centers are dedicated to providing quality child care and early education for your children.

Taking a tour will allow you to see the care and dedication that go into nurturing your children.

**Meet the Dedicated Staff**

The staff at the CDCs are highly trained and dedicated professionals who are passionate about early childhood education. They are committed to ensuring each child receives personalized care and attention, promoting their physical, social, emotional, and cognitive development.

**Engaging Programs**

The centers offer a variety of age-appropriate programs and activities that cater to the unique needs and interests of each child. From interactive playtime to structured learning sessions, children are encouraged to explore, discover, and learn in a fun and supportive environment.

**Safety and Security**

The safety and well-being of your children are top priority. The centers are equipped with modern security features, including secure entry points and constant supervision to ensure a safe environment for all.

**Community Focus**

Visiting a CDC also provides insight into the strong sense of community among military families. You'll witness firsthand the camaraderie and support that exist within these centers, making them more than just childcare facilities but integral parts of the military community.

**Tours are not available at all locations. Contact your local CDC to schedule a tour.**

## Child Care Resources
Providing flexible child care solutions for families.

### Full-time Child Care

Supporting families with children ages 6 weeks to 5 years, ensuring age-appropriate learning guided by the Early Learning Matters (ELM) Curriculum.

**Curriculum:**

All Child Development Centers use the Early Learning Matters (ELM) curriculum as the primary classroom curriculum. ELM is based on the latest research on child development and best practices in early education and care. ELM offers a comprehensive, developmentally appropriate approach to meaningful learning for all children featuring:

* A whole child focus on skills that bolster school readiness and life success.
* Developmentally sequenced activities that embed strategies for individualizing learning.
* Evidence-informed, friendly-to-use resources for classroom staff and families.

At the heart of the ELM curriculum are activity plans that build on children's pathways of development in five infant/toddler areas and eight preschool areas. The plans support growth and development with a range of active learning opportunities that include careful attention to differences in children's abilities and interests.

**Accreditation & Certification:**

CDCs are required to be nationally accredited and must pass an annual Department of Defense inspection to obtain a certificate to operate.

### School Age Care

Fostering the development, resilience, and promote lifelong skills for school age children.

School Age Care (SAC) offers vital support to military families. To enroll your children into SAC, visit the [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/).

Key Benefits:

**Safe and Structured Environment**

Provides a secure, supervised setting for children ages 5-12, ensuring peace of mind for parents during work hours and deployments.

**Academic Support**

Offers homework assistance, tutoring, and educational activities to help children excel in school and develop lifelong learning habits.

**Social Development**

Encourages children to build friendships, improve communication skills, and develop teamwork through group activities and games.

**Resilience Building**

Promotes emotional well-being and adaptability by offering programs that help children manage the unique challenges of military life, such as frequent moves and parental deployments.

**Recreational Activities**

Provides engaging, age-appropriate recreational activities that promote physical fitness, creativity, and exploration.

**Support for Military Readiness**

Enables military parents to focus on their mission, knowing their children are in a supportive, enriching environment.

**Affordable and Flexible Care Options**

Offers cost-effective programs tailored to the needs of military families, with flexible care schedules to accommodate varying work hours.

**Connection to MCCS Resources**

Provides access to other MCCS programs, such as Family Advocacy, Youth Sports, and the Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP), ensuring comprehensive support for families.

School Age Care programs are designed to strengthen military families and help children thrive, fostering a sense of community and stability within the Marine Corps lifestyle.

### Hourly Child Care

Hourly child care is available for those moments when you need to run errands, enjoy a lunch date, or alone time to re-energize.

Hourly child care may be available on your installation Child Development Centers (CDC) for an hourly rate per child.

* Hourly child care does not require parents to make a request on [militarychildcare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/).
* Parents need to complete and submit the CDC packet and provide the necessary supporting documents to register their child.
* This service is provided based on space availability or may not be offered at your installation.
* Contact your local installation's CDC for availability.

## Family Support Resources
Connecting families to essential tools and resources.

### PCS Workshop

Offering valuable guidance and resources to help you plan and navigate your move to a new duty station.

The Permanent Change of Station (PCS) Workshop is designed to guide Marines and their families through every step of the relocation process. Whether it's your first move or one of many, our workshop provides valuable insights and resources to help you transition with ease.

Nine reasons to attend a PCS Workshop:

1. **Policy** - Per MCO 1754.10B, attending the PCS Workshop is required for a smooth transition to your new duty station.
2. **Installation-specific Information and Contacts** - Get valuable information about your new installation, including key contacts and local services.
3. **Household Goods Weight Allowances & Entitlements** - Learn about your weight allowances for household goods and what entitlements you can access during your move.
4. **Travel Allowances, Budget, and Government Card** - Understand your travel allowances, how to budget for the move, and how to use your government travel card.
5. **Moving with Pets** - Receive guidance on transporting pets, quarantine regulations, and other related requirements.
6. **School Liaison & Exceptional Family Member Program Resources** - Access support for school enrollment and resources for family members with special needs.
7. **Spouse Employment Opportunities** - Discover job search assistance and career development resources for spouses.
8. **Personalized Relocation Plan & Online Relocation Resources** - Create a customized relocation plan and explore online resources to streamline your move.
9. **Sponsorship** - As per MCO 1320.11H, learn how to request a sponsor to help you adjust and settle into your new duty station.

Don't move alone. Contact your [Information, Referral, and Relocation](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/information-referral-and-relocation) specialist for PCS Workshop information.

### School Liaison

Sharing essential information and support to navigate local school systems and ensure a smooth transition for your children.

The School Liaison is a vital resource for Marines and their families new to an installation, helping to ensure a seamless transition for children into local schools. By providing essential information and support, the School Liaison assists families in navigating educational options and addressing any concerns related to their child's education.

School Liaison support includes:

* **School Enrollment** - Guidance on enrolling children in local schools and understanding registration requirements.
* **Local School Information** - Up-to-date resources about school districts, programs, and options available in the area.
* **Home School Information** - Assisting families with guidance on registering with the DoDEA schools.
* **Exceptional Family Member Support** - Help with navigating the special education process and accessing available services.
* **Transition Assistance** - Resources for families moving to a new area, including information on school calendars and schedules.

These services help ensure that children receive the support they need for a successful educational experience in their new community.

For more information about support and services, visit the [School Liaison](https://yuma.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-liaison) webpage on the MCCS website.

### Exceptional Family Member Program

Supporting military families with special medical or educational needs, ensuring they have access to necessary services.

The Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) is essential for service members and their families with special needs, providing support and resources to ensure a smooth transition to a new installation.

EFMP helps families navigate the challenges associated with relocating by connecting them to specialized services and community resources tailored to their unique circumstances.

EFMP Services Available Include:

* **Enrollment Assistance** - Guidance on enrolling in the EFMP and understanding program requirements.
* **Specialized Support Services** - Access to resources for medical, educational, and emotional support tailored to family members with special needs.
* **Transition Assistance** - Help with relocating to a new area, including information on local schools, medical facilities, and community services.
* **Advocacy and Resources** - Connection to advocacy services and local support groups to assist families in accessing necessary care and benefits.
* **Workshops and Training** - Opportunities for families to participate in workshops focused on managing special needs and navigating available resources.

Learn more about how EFMP supports you and your family by visiting [EFMP](https://usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/exceptional-family-member-program).

### Marine Corps Family Team Building

Offering comprehensive support to the entire military community through a variety of workshops and training programs.

Eligibility for participation in the Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB) programs extend to individuals across various segments of the military community. This includes:

* Active Duty Service Members: Including all branches of the military, all ranks.
* Department of Defense (DoD) Employees
* Spouses of Military Personnel

MCFTB is designed to enhance the resilience, readiness, and well-being of all members of the Marine Corps community, including service members, spouses, children, extended family members, command leaders, units, and support personnel.

**How to get started with MCFTB:**

1. **Identify Individual Needs:** Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more. MCFTB professionals can help you identify your specific needs.
2. **Connect with MCFTB:** Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone. They can provide guidance on available programs, workshops, and resources that best suit your needs.
3. **Attend Workshops and Classes:** Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation. These could include pre-deployment briefs, relationship-enhancement classes, pre-marital and marital workshops, relocation assistance workshops, family readiness seminars, financial planning classes, and more.
4. **Connect with Other Families:** Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms. Building connections with other families can provide valuable support and camaraderie.

### New Parent Support

Offering home visits, classes, and resources to help new and expecting parents build confidence, manage stress, and care for their growing families.

New Parent Support offers guidance, education, and support to our Marines, their families throughout our military community. Eligible participants can access resources provided by New Parent Support.

Eligible Participants:

* Parents with children up to age 5
* DoD Spouses
* DoD Families

Connect with your New Parent Support office to begin your journey with our caring professionals.

### Information, Referral, and Relocation

Connecting Marines and their families with resources, support, and guidance to ease transitions and enhance readiness throughout their military journey.

**Information, Referral, and Relocation (IR&R) services** to support Marines and their families through life's transitions, whether it's a Permanent Change of Station (PCS), deployment, or other major milestones. These services are designed to ease the challenges of relocation and connect families to valuable resources within their community.

**Key Services Provided:**

* **Welcome Aboard Brief** - Provides newcomers with essential information about their new installation, local community, and available resources.
* **Relocation Assistance** - Offers one-on-one support for PCS moves, including help with planning, moving tips, and checklists to ensure a smooth transition.
* **Requesting a Sponsor** - Connects Marines and their families with trained sponsors to provide personalized support and guidance during relocation.
* **Lending Locker** - Supplies temporary household items, such as kitchenware and small appliances, to help families settle in while awaiting their belongings.
* **Base Housing Support** - Offers guidance on housing options, including on-base housing, rental listings, and off-base accommodations.
* **DEERS and ID Card Assistance** - Provides information and support for enrolling in the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS) and obtaining necessary ID cards.
* **Child Care and School Liaison Support** - Helps families find child care and connects them with School Liaison Officers for school registration and educational resources.
* **Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) Support** - Ensures families with special needs have access to tailored relocation assistance and resources at their new duty station.

**Benefits of IR&R Services**

* Reduces stress and uncertainty associated with frequent moves.
* Enhances readiness by ensuring families are well-informed and prepared.
* Strengthens connections within the Marine Corps community.
* Provides access to resources that promote resilience and stability.

Whether you're transitioning to a new duty station or looking for local resources, IR&R services are here to support you every step of the way.

## Life Skill-building Resources
Developing skills for personal and professional growth.

### Budgeting for Child Care

Learning how to budget the expense of child care can help you and your family reach your financial goals.

The professionals at [Personal Financial Management](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/personal-financial-management) can help you prepare for financial changes by offering guidance on budgeting, saving, and managing child care expenses.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

* Blended Retirement System (BRS)
* Car Buying
* Consumer Awareness
* Continuation Pay
* Couple Financial Counseling
* Credit Report and Credit Score Analysis Saving and Investing
* Credit / Debt Management
* Developing a Spending Plan
* Financial Education Action Points (FEAP)
* Individual Financial Counseling

### Managing Stress

Life challenges can be stressful on you and your family. We are here to help.

The Community Counseling Program utilizes a holistic approach to support individuals, children, couples, and families. Our professional clinicians provide solutions designed to meet your specific needs in the following areas:

* Relationship Concerns
* Work Stressors
* Life Stressors
* Trauma
* EAS/PCS and Challenges Related to Transition
* Grief and Loss
* Sadness
* Worry
* Deployment Cycle Stressors and Reintegration
* Adjustment
* Crisis Intervention
* Sleep Hygiene
* Parent-Child Communication

Establish a connection with professionals from your Community Counseling center and discover a successful journey toward overcoming life's challenges.

[Community Counseling](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling)

## Frequently Asked Question (FAQs)
Quick answers to common questions.

### What ages does the Child Development Center serve?

The Child Development Center provides child care to children from 6 weeks to 5 years old.

### How do I enroll my child in the Child Development Centers?

Enrollment is completed through [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/), where you can create an account, select your preferences, and join the waitlist.

### How are fees determined?

Fees are based on total family income and follow the Department of Defense fee structure.

### What types of activities does the Child Development Center offer?

The Child Development Center provides age-appropriate activities that promote cognitive, social, emotional, and physical development through a structured curriculum.

### Who should I contact if I have additional questions?

You can contact the Child Development Center office at your installation for further assistance.

pages.text:
# Family Child Care

We provide your child, aged 6 weeks to 12 years, with a nurturing environment, that supports their development and helps them thrive within the community.

## Getting Started is Easy
Navigating steps to successfully register for child care.

### Registration Guidance

Welcome to Family Child Care (FCC), where your child will learn, grow, and thrive in a safe and supportive environment. FCC Providers are highly trained and regulated, including thorough background checks and monthly inspections. FCC providers create a sense of belonging for families and support them in developing their child(ren)'s positive self-worth. We're excited to be part of your community.

Registration is quick and easy—simply follow the steps below.

1. **Go to** [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/)
   - Set up an account if you don't already have one.
   - Add your child's information and request care at your installation.
2. **Join the Waitlist**
   - If space is not immediately available, your child will be placed on a waitlist.
   - You will receive an offer via email to inform you when a spot opens up.
   - If you are placed on a waitlist you have the option of contacting [MCCYN](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome/mccyn) which provides fee assistance to offset the costs of community-based care.
3. **Accept the Offer**
   - Once you receive an offer, follow the instructions to accept it within the given timeframe.
   - If you don't respond within the timeframe, the offer is removed, but you may request reactivation with supporting details if eligible.
4. **Complete the Registration Process**
   - After accepting the offer, you will receive forms to complete.
   - Provide necessary documents, such as proof of eligibility, immunization records, and emergency contacts.
5. **Attend Parent Orientation**
   - You will be required to attend an orientation to review program policies and expectations.
6. **Start Care**
   - Once all paperwork is submitted and fees are processed, your child can begin attending the program.

If you need help getting started please contact our Resource and Referral office. They can answer questions and guide you through the process.

## Eligibility
Exploring the requirements and determining if you qualify.

Family Child Care (FCC) provides a safe, enriching environment for children while supporting the unique needs of military families. We proudly serve those who serve by offering quality care that fosters learning, resilience, and connection. FCC providers establish their own schedules and may provide care outside standard work hours.

**Family Child Care is available to children of:**

- Active-duty Service Members
- DoD Civilian Employees
- Reservists
- DoD contractors

**Children:**

- Must be between the ages of 6 weeks to 12 years old.

**Enrollment:**

- Enrollment is guided by DoD priorities. Supplanting does not apply to FCC. To secure a spot, families are encouraged to register early, as availability may vary depending on demand.

**Department of Defense Policies:**

- [DoDI 6060.02](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=c8ad90d5-2d16-44a7-95b6-224de21dfd54&v=1)
- [MCO 1710.30A](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=a98aa33f-1d48-4466-8530-c790d725bfed&v=1)

For more information on eligibility, priority placement, and registration requirements, please contact our Resource and Referral office.

## MilitaryChildCare.com
Registering online is easy and convenient.

MilitaryChildCare.com makes it easy to find and request Family Child Care (FCC), giving you peace of mind knowing your child is in a safe and supportive environment.

With just one online account, you can explore program options, submit a request, and manage your childcare needs from anywhere. Spaces are assigned based on DoD priority placement, so registering early ensures you have the best chance of securing care when you need it.

Start today by visiting [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome).

## Child Care Support
Exploring child care opportunities.

### I Need Child Care

Family Child Care is a great child care choice offered right in your community. Certified providers care for small groups of children in their own homes, either on the installation or nearby. Think of it as quality child care in a comfortable, home-like setting.

**Flexible, Home-Based Child Care for Your Family**

Family Child Care (FCC) offers a safe, nurturing, and home-like environment for children ages 6 weeks to 12 years. With small group sizes and flexible hours, FCC provides personalized care that fits your family's schedule, including full-time, part-time, evening, and weekend options. Licensed providers are trained to support your child's development while ensuring a warm, engaging atmosphere.

**Eligibility & Requirements:**

Family Child Care (FCC) is designed to support military families by providing high-quality, home-based child care. Eligibility is based on priority and availability.

- Active-Duty Service Members
- Department of Defense (DoD) Civilians
- Reservists & National Guard Members
- Retirees
- DoD Contractors

To ensure a safe and developmentally appropriate environment, children enrolled in the Family Child Care (FCC) program must meet the following requirements:

**Age Requirements**

- Children must be between 6 weeks and 12 years old to enroll in FCC.
- School-age children (up to 12 years) may attend before/after school care, full-day care during school breaks, and summer programs.

**Health & Immunization Requirements**

- All children must have up-to-date immunization records, including age-appropriate vaccines as required by DoD and state regulations.

**Special Needs & Accommodations**

- The CYP behavior specialist, CYP nurse, and FCC providers work together to assess and accommodate children with special needs.
- Parents must disclose any medical, developmental, or dietary requirements during registration to ensure proper care and support.

If you have any question please contact our Resource and Referral office.

### I Want to Provide Child Care

As a Family Child Care provider, you'll offer safe, high-quality care for military children while enjoying flexible hours, professional training, and the ability to care for your own children at home. MCCS provides free training, support, and resources to help you succeed.

Start your journey today—make a difference in the lives of military families while building your own career! Contact your local Family Child Care office to learn more.

**Why Become an FCC Provider?**

- Run your own home-based business while supporting military families.
- Enjoy flexible hours and the ability to care for your own children at home.
- Receive training and support at no cost, including CPR, First Aid, and child development courses.
- Gain access to resources and equipment, including a lending library of toys and materials.
- Participate in the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program to receive meal reimbursements.

**Eligibility Requirements:**

- Must be at least 18 years old.
- Have a high school diploma or equivalent.
- Reside in government housing or approved off-base housing.
- Pass a comprehensive background check for all household members over 18.
- Complete a health screening for yourself and any family members who will be in the home.

**Steps to Get Started:**

1. Contact your local Family Child Care office to learn more about the application process and training requirements.
2. Download and complete the FCC Application or be obtained the application at the [Resource and Referral](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/information-referral-and-relocation) office. Application requires background checks.
3. Complete a family interview (provider applicant and spouse)
4. If interested in processing with the certification process, background checks are initiated.
5. Pay a non-refundable $50 training fee at Family Child Care office which covers the cost of the CPR/First Aid training. Training fees are not required at all locations. Contact the Resource and Referral office about training fees.
6. Attend FCC Provider initial training - 40-hours (one-week)
7. Complete health requirements for all household members
8. Set up home in accordance with regulatory requirements.
9. Home inspection by Fire, Safety & Sanitation.
10. Quality Review Board.
11. Documentation sent to SJA regarding successfully completion of requirements (to obtain authorization to operate a home business).
12. (Upon SJA approval) Provider files Housing Addendum, notifying Family Housing of FCC business
13. Purchase Liability Insurance.
14. Upon clearance to start, Resource & Referral will assist in setting up provider's profile on [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/)
15. Final walk-through by FCC staff.
16. Open for business!
17. Be committed to attending ongoing training sessions to guarantee the highest quality of care for children. This includes monthly evening training.

Homes should obtain certification from the command if they provide more than 10 "child care hours" per week. For instance, if a resident looks after two children for five hours, it amounts to 10 hours of child care. Homes that operate outside this framework without certification will be deemed unauthorized. Enforcement against such unauthorized care will be as per the Housing Office rules and regulations. Detailed information can be found on page 6 of the Resident handbook.

The FCC program is not only about providing care but also about ensuring that the caregivers are well-trained, certified, and provide a safe and nurturing environment for the children. The command plays an active role in monitoring and certifying providers, ensuring the best care for the children enrolled in the FCC program.

If you have any questions please contact our Resource and Referral office.

## Life Skill-building Resources
Developing essential skills for personal and professional growth.

### School Liaison

Providing essential information and support for a positive academic experience for your children.

School Liaison support include:

- **School Enrollment** - Guidance on enrolling children in local schools and understanding registration requirements.
- **Local School Information** - Up-to-date resources about school districts, programs, and options available in the area.
- **Home School Information** - Assisting families with guidance on their local school district homeschool requirements.
- **Special Education Support** - Help with navigating the special education process and accessing available services to include warm hand offs to EFMP.
- **Transition Assistance** - Resources for families moving to a new area, including information on school calendars and schedules.

For more information about support and services, visit the [School Liaison](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-liaison) webpage on the MCCS website.

### Exceptional Family Member Program

EFMP Services Available Include:

- **Enrollment Assistance** - Guidance on enrolling in the EFMP and understanding program requirements.
- **Specialized Support Services** - Access to resources for medical, educational, and emotional support tailored to family members with special needs.
- **Transition Assistance** - Help with relocating to a new area, including information on local schools, medical facilities, and community services.
- **Advocacy and Resources** - Connection to advocacy services and local support groups to assist families in accessing necessary care and benefits.
- **Workshops and Training** - Opportunities for families to participate in workshops focused on managing special needs and navigating available resources.

### Budgeting Your Child Care

Learning how to save and manage expenses during and after a move.

The professionals at [Personal Financial Management](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/personal-financial-management) can help you prepare for financial changes by offering guidance on budgeting, saving, and managing educational expenses.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

- Blended Retirement System (BRS)
- Car Buying
- Consumer Awareness
- Continuation Pay
- Couple Financial Counseling
- Credit Report and Credit Score Analysis Saving and Investing
- Credit / Debt Management
- Developing a Spending Plan
- Financial Education Action Points (FEAP)
- Individual Financial Counseling
- Major Purchases
- Military Pay & Benefits
- Retirement Planning
- Survivor Benefits Plan
- Thrift Savings Plan
- Understanding Military Retirement Benefits

### Marine Corps Family Team Building

Strengthening the resilience, readiness, and well-being of our military community.

[Marine Corps Family Team Building](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/marine-corps-family-team-building) (MCFTB) is designed to enhance the resilience, readiness, and well-being of all members of the Marine Corps community, including service members, spouses, children, extended family members, command leaders, units, and support personnel.

How to get started with MCFTB:

- **Identify Individual Needs** - Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more. MCFTB professionals can help you identify your specific needs.
- **Connect with MCFTB** - Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone. They can provide guidance on available programs, workshops, and resources that best suit your needs.
- **Attend Workshops and Classes** - Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation. These could include pre-deployment briefs, relationship-enhancement classes, pre-marital and marital workshops, relocation assistance workshops, family readiness seminars, financial planning classes, and more.
- **Connect with Other Families** - Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms. Building connections with other families can provide valuable support and camaraderie.

### Libraries

Discovering resources that provide access to knowledge, innovation, and creativity.

The [Library](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/libraries) is a great resource for families and school-age children, offering books, educational programs, and activities that support learning and growth. Whether you're looking for homework help, fun storytimes, or a quiet place to read and explore, the Library provides a welcoming space for children to develop their love of learning. Stop by and discover all the ways we support your family!

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

- **Children's Collection** - A diverse selection of picture books, chapter books, movies, and audiobooks designed for young readers.
- **Summer Reading Program** - Featuring free activities and incentives to encourage a love of reading during the summer months.
- **Storytime Kits** - Themed kits that include books and activities, allowing families to enjoy storytime at their convenience.
- **Educational Programs and Activities** - Various events and workshops that enrich your children's learning experiences.
- **Access to Digital Resources** - Online materials, including e-books and educational databases, to support learning and exploration. Visit the [DoD MWR Virtual Library](https://marines.dodmwrlibraries.org/).

### Guiding Growth & Resilience

Helping children thrive within the military community.

[Community Counseling](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling) provides support to ease this transition by offering emotional support, stress management strategies, and adjustment counseling. Counselors help families navigate the challenges of relocation, offering guidance on coping with change, building resilience, and connecting with local resources.

Through individual and family counseling, the program helps create a smooth transition, strengthening the overall well-being of military families.

Life Skills Development Resources:

- Relationship Concerns
- Work Stressors
- Life Stressors
- Trauma
- EAS/PCS and Challenges Related to Transition
- Grief and Loss
- Sadness
- Worry
- Deployment Cycle Stressors and Reintegration
- Adjustment
- Crisis Intervention
- Sleep Hygiene
- Parent-Child Communication

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
**Who can become a Family Child Care provider?**

Any military spouse or eligible individual 18 years or older who lives in base housing or approved off-base housing can apply. Providers must complete training, background checks, and home inspections to become licensed.

**What are the benefits of becoming an FCC provider?**

FCC providers run their own home-based business, set their own hours, care for their own children while earning income, receive free training and resources, and participate in the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program.

**What are the requirements for enrolling a child in FCC?**

Children must be between 6 weeks and 12 years old, have up-to-date immunizations, and meet health and safety requirements. Families must register through MilitaryChildCare.com or their local Resource & Referral (R&R) office.

**How is Family Child Care different from a Child Development Center (CDC)?**

FCC provides home-based care in smaller groups, offering more personalized attention, flexible hours, and a family-like setting compared to larger Child Development Centers (CDCs).

**How do I find an FCC provider for my child?**

Parents can search for available FCC providers and request care through MilitaryChildCare.com or contact their local FCC office or Resource & Referral (R&R) office for assistance.

# New Parent Support

The New Parent Support Program (NPSP) is a professional team of social workers, counselors, and registered nurses who provide confidential education and support to Marine families who are expecting or raising children aged 0-5 years old.

## Program Benefits
- Be prepared for parenthood
- Become more confident
- Understand your child's development
- Develop common ground with your spouse in the area of parenting
- Improve your relationship with your children
- Make parenting fun
- Be a better parent to your children
- Feel more at home in the military community

## Who's Eligible
All military families expecting or with a child under six years of age are eligible to participate free of charge in all services offered.

## What if we are not new parents?
Even if you have been raising your family for a few years, new ages and stages bring different challenges. Often, adding a brother or sister to the family presents a real change for everyone. The New Parent Support Program offers you the opportunity to express your concerns and ask questions about babies, young children and family relationships.

## Home Visits
Are confidential and can take place in the home, the New Parent Support office, or any other convenient and comfortable location. The evidence-based Parents as Teachers curriculum is utilized during home visits.

## Baby Boot Camp
This course offers expectant parents the basic information and tools needed to provide loving care for their newborn. Join us for hands-on practice as we learn and discuss:

Basic infant care, birth plants, self-care, bathing, feeding, diapering, pre- and post-partum emotions, labor and delivery, infant growth and development, infant safety, attachment, bonding, soothing a crying baby, and more!

**Locations Available:** Mainside, 13 Area, San Onofre, and Temecula*

*Baby Boot Camp is offered bimonthly at the [Tricare Outpatient Clinic in Temecula](https://maps.app.goo.gl/6VxkNVVodX9AXtbQ6).

## Baby Bump Bags
Are you or your spouse expecting? Congratulations!

Pick up your Welcome Baby Bag From your DRC, URC, or MFLC today.

Don't forget to check out and sign up for all the classes and resources available through the New Parent Support Program.

## Mothers in Transition
New and expectant mothers, active duty or dependent spouses have a safe and confidential space to:

- Learn about and prevent postpartum depression and anxiety
- Learn and practice new ways to nurture yourself
- Gain support from others to cope with the transition to motherhood the good, the bad, and the ugly
- Manage your feelings and thoughts to feel better

## Parenting Class
A 9-week, court-approved parenting class series for parents with children under the age of 6. Topics include:

- Safety
- Communication
- Discipline
- Self-esteem
- Family Structure

Parenting class offers parents the tools to raise healthy, happy, and cooperative children. Join us as we learn the skills to help build a trusting and loving relationship, and guide behavior with clear communication, effective limit-setting, and the use of consequences.

Class #1 Caring & Connecting with Our Children
Class #2 Development & Temperament
Class #3 Protecting Our Children
Class #4 Emotions: More Than Just Angry & Hungry
Class #5 Self-Esteem & Cooperation
Class #6 Effective Communication: Speaking a Child's Language

Classes are held on Tuesdays from 1pm-2:30pm at Marine & Family Programs West (BLDG 202860) off San Jacinto Road. No pre-registration is required. Parents only please, as childcare is not provided at this time.

All classes must be completed within one year to receive a certificate of completion. Please check the events calendar for locations, dates, and times.

Join us every Monday at 10am to have fun, make friends, and learn about parenting topics like play, emotional regulation, and setting limits.

For more information, please call (760) 725-3884.
