## Education Services and Support
Successfully reach your goals with tools and resources.

## Testing Services
Using testing resources to help you earn college credits and certifications.

Voluntary Education offers testing services in the areas of military professional testing, high school equivalency (GED), college proctored testing, career entrance qualification exams, as well as professional certification and licensure testing.

Testing services are available at little to no cost and are designed to support your educational and professional development.

Contact the Education Center for more information on testing resources and support.

**Military Testing**

All tests are by appointment only. Service members must register in advance. On the day of the exam, service members must be in the uniform of the day and show their military ID at check-in. For more information or to schedule an appointment, contact the Education Center.

- Armed Forces Classification Test (AFCT)
- Aviation Selection Test Battery (ASTB)
- Defense Language Aptitude Battery (DLAB)
- Defense Language Proficiency Test (DLPT)
- Oral Proficiency Interview (OPI)
- Test of Adult Basic Education (TABE)

Not all tests are offered at all locations. Please contact the education center for availability.

**CLEP and DSST Exams**

- College Level Examination Program (CLEP): CLEP now offers test takers the option to take a CLEP exam with remote proctoring. Each CLEP exam taken with remote proctoring has the same timing, content, format, and on-screen experience as the test you would take at a CLEP test center. You will be proctored remotely by a human proctor. Visit https://clep.collegeboard.org/about-remote-proctoring/take-clep-exam-remote-proctoring for specific information.
- DANTES Subject Standardized Tests (DSST): DSST does allow remote proctoring of exams for eligible service members. Civilian and non-eligible military test takers cannot take an exam via Remote Proctor. Visit https://www.prometric.com/exams/dantes for specific information.

**Graduate Records Exam (GRE)**

- Graduate Records Exam (GRE)
- Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT)
- Praxis I and II

**General Education Diploma (GED)**

To schedule an exam date, you must create an account by registering on [GED Testing Service](https://www.ged.com) and selecting the jurisdiction you are testing under. You can call the GED Testing Service at the following:

- 1-877-EXAM-GED (877-392-6433) (North & South Americas Region)
- +85-2-3077-4923 (Asia Pacific Region)
- (toll) +44 204-602-9757 (Europe, Middle Eastern)

Not all tests are offered at all locations. Please contact the Education Center for availability.

**GED Study Materials**

GED study materials can be found at the local library or online. Here are some of the online resources to get you started.

- Free practice tests and e-books are available from [EBSCO Learning Express](https://www.learningexpresshub.com/ProductEngine/LELIndex.html#/learningexpresslibrary/libraryhome) (DoD MWR Library). Contact your local MCCS library for access code.
- The Online Academic Skills Course (OASC) helps build and refresh basic math and verbal skills. Access to OASC is free for the military community and can be accessed by creating an account at [DANTES](https://dantes.petersons.com/).
- [MyGED® Dashboard](https://ged.com/): Learn more about the test, policies, and try sample test questions.
- Official [GED Marketplace](https://www.GEDmarketplace.com)

**SAT and ACT**

- American College Testing (ACT)
- Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT)

For both the SAT and ACT you will first need to register and create an account with [College Board](https://mysat.collegeboard.org/login). Please visit the appropriate websites for information as well as registration deadlines.

Students can request to have their official ACT results sent to the Education Center. Contact the Education Center for the ACT Site Code.

**Digital SAT**

The SAT can also be taken digitally through [SAT Suite College Board](https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/sat). Before you take the digital SAT, you will need to download Bluebook on your device.

## Joint Service Transcripts (JST)
Converting your military training into college credits to save time and money.

The Joint Service Transcripts (JST) program provides you with an official record of your military training and experience, converting it into civilian academic credit.

The JST includes courses, certifications, and job experience you gained during military service and is used by colleges and universities to assess and award valid credits toward degree programs.

This helps you save time and money by earning credit for what you've already learned in the military and facilitating your educational and career advancement.

Credits awarded from the Joint Services Transcript (JST) are determined solely by the individual learning institution. Not all credits may be accepted, and they might not align with your long-term career goals. The Education Center is here to guide you in selecting the best school to support your career plans.

For more information, visit [Joint Service Transcript](https://jst.doded.mil/jst/) or contact the Education Center.

## United Services Military Apprenticeship Program (USMAP)
Earning an apprenticeship certification while performing your military duties.

Take advantage of the United Services Military Apprenticeship Program (USMAP) and earn an apprenticeship certification while performing your mitary duties.

This Department of Defense-sponsored program allows you to earn a Department of Labor-recognized apprenticeship certification while performing your regular military duties.

USMAP combines on-the-job training with academic instruction to help service members gain valuable skills, enhance their career prospects, and earn credentials that are recognized by civilian employers.

The program is offered at no cost and covers a wide range of occupations aligned with military specialties, helping Marines transition smoothly into the civilian workforce.

Learn more about the apprenticeship certification at [USMAP](https://usmap.osd.mil/index.htm).

## Online Academic Skills Course (OASC)
Building your academic skills to achieve long-term career success.

The Online Academic Skills Course (OASC) helps you improve essential skills in math, reading, and writing. This free, self-paced program is designed to enhance academic performance, prepare for exams, and support career development, making it a valuable tool for those pursuing further education or career advancement.

The OASC can help service members prepare to take the Armed Forces Classifications Test (AFCT).

Visit [DANTES](https://dantes.petersons.com/) to learn more about OASC.

## Marine Corps COOL
Obtaining credentials, certifications, and licenses based on your military skills and experience.

Marines interested in the [COOL](https://www.cool.osd.mil/usmc/index.html) program should visit the Education Center and speak to an advisor to explore available credentials, understand the application process, and get started on obtaining valuable certifications and licenses.

## Career Path Decide
Discovering careers that align with your military background, education, and civilian work experience.

Career Path Decide is an assessment tool that can help you focus your efforts and resources on a specific goal, leading to greater fulfillment and success. Taking the four surveys on skills, lifestyle, interests, and values will help you identify your strengths and passions and set long-term goals. The results can even help you find the right credentials and/or degree programs needed to fill experience and education gaps, making you more qualified, prepared, and marketable.

Learn more about the assessment and how it can help you at [Career Path Decide](https://www.careerpathdecide.org/).

## Spouse Works
Bringing together trusted career and education support in one place with no changes to services, eligibility or partnerships.

## Leadership Scholar Program
Attending college or university after you transition from the Marine Corps.

## Financial Resources
Achieve your goals with expert financial services and support.

## Personal Financial Management
Helping you prepare financially by offering guidance and resources on budgeting, saving, and managing educational expenses.

## Federal Student Aid
Reaching your personal and professional development goals with support from financial aid. ([FAFSA](https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa))

## Tuition Assistance
Exploring financial aid opportunities that support your education journey.

Tuition Assistance (TA) is a higher education benefit available to you as an active duty service member if you are pursuing or want to pursue college-level coursework. You can receive up to $4,500 per fiscal year to cover up to 100% of tuition and eligible fees toward a college-level diploma, credential, certificate, or degree program.

First time applicants should do the following:

1. **Personal Readiness Seminar (PRS)** — Completed either in person or online. Online training availalbe at JKO. The online course is J3OP- US1395-Personal Readiness Seminar (PRS) Survival Skills (2 hrs).
2. **Complete the USMC TA Brief** — Visit your local education center for dates, location, and registration information.
3. **Upload Your Career Path Decide Results** — Complete the Skills and Interests Surveys at Career Path Decide and upload a screenshot to your TA portal.
4. **Visit the Education Center** — Education Center advisors can assist with selecting the best academic program for your educational and career goals.
5. **Enroll in a School** — Request a degree plan, select your first class, send transcripts, and send your Joint Service Transcript obtained from JST. An official degree plan must be uploaded to your TA portal after completing four courses or before taking two classes at a time.
6. **Identify Your TA Command Approver** — Be sure to get command approver's email and phone number to add to your TA portal later.
7. **Log-in to Your Tuition Assistance (TA) Portal** — You can log into your TA portal by visiting [Navy Education and Training Commmand](https://myeducation.netc.navy.mil/webta/). Complete your "Update Your Profile" tab with your contact and command approver information.
8. **Submit Your TA Request** — On your TA portal, you can submit your request for your class. You must include specific course information and term dates.
9. **Forward to your Command Approver** — When you submit your request to your command approver, they will be able to review your course information and approve or deny your request. Once your command approver has approved your request, the Education Center will review your request for eligibility and authorize a TA voucher. Be sure to allow time for the approval process as TA cannot be authorized after the start date of the class.
10. **Pay For Your Class** — After your TA request has been authorized, print the voucher from your TA portal, sign the voucher, and deliver it to the school to make tuition payment.

**Tuition Assistance Approval**

Tuition Assistance (TA) can only be approved for courses starting within 60 days and needs to be applied for each term. To apply for TA for another term, applicants should repeat steps 8-10. Only 2 classes are funded at a time. Only 1 class is funded for first time users, applicants with a GPA below 2.5 or those who failed their last class.

**Payment:**

You can receive up to $4,500 per fiscal year (Oct 1 - Sep 30). TA covers up to $250 per semester hour, $166.67 per quarter hour, and $16.67 per clock hour. Classes you fail (grade D, F, W, or I) will require repayment. For full details, check the NAVMAC or contact your Education Center.

**Reimbursements**

Marines who fail to complete a course successfully must reimburse received TA funds. TA funds are recouped from Marines for "D" and "F"/fail grades, unresolved "I"/Incomplete, or courses from which the Marine voluntarily withdrew, resulting in a "W" grade.

**Waivers**

Waivers for repayment are available for students who withdraw due to duty, medical, or emergency circumstances. The waiver request should contain supporting documentation including, where appropriate, temporary assignment of duty (TAD) or permanent change of station (PCS) orders. Include a descriptive narrative explaining the change beyond individual control and unknown at the time of the TA request. The Education Services Officer determines if justification for a waiver is warranted, and if so, forwards the waiver onto [Naval Education and Training Professional Development Center](https://www.netc.navy.mil/NETPDC/) (NETPDC) with additional support statements. Contact your local Education Center for more information.

**Tuition Assistance Restrictions**

- TA cannot be used for flight training.
- TA is not available if you're in duty-under-instruction status or an officer accession program with full-time civilian institution instruction.
- You cannot use TA for the same course that was previously funded.
- TA will not be approved after the drop/add period or late registration deadline

For more information, reach out to your Education Center.

## GI Bill
Empowering you to advance your skills, further your education, and achieve long-term success.

The GI Bills provide you with valuable educational benefits to support your personal and professional growth. Whether through the Post-9/11 GI Bill or the Montgomery GI Bill, you can access funding for tuition, housing, and other expenses, making higher education and career training more accessible.

**Post-9/11 GI Bill**

- Available to service members who served after Sept. 10, 2001, with at least 90 days of active duty. Service members will only earn 50% of benefit with only 90 days of service.
- Covers up to 100% of tuition and fees for public schools (or up to a capped amount for private schools), provides a monthly housing allowance, and includes a stipend for books and supplies.
- Allows eligible service members to transfer benefits to dependents under certain conditions.
- Benefits are generally available for 15 years after discharge.

**Montgomery GI Bill**

- Requires active duty service for at least two years and an enrollment in the program with a monthly contribution during service.
- Pays a set monthly amount to the service member, based on the number of classes taken, without a housing allowance or book stipend.
- Does not offer the option to transfer benefits.
- Benefits must be used within 10 years of discharge

For more information visit the [U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs](https://www.va.gov/education/).

## My Career Advancement Account (MyCAA)
Providing up to $4,000 of tuition assistance to eligible military spouses.

The My Career Advancement Account Scholarship pays tuition costs for education and training courses and examinations leading to an associate degree (excluding associate degrees in general studies, liberal arts and interdisciplinary studies that do not have a concentration). The scholarship also covers the costs for obtaining a license, certificate, or certification at an accredited college, university or technical school in the United States or approved testing organization that expands employment or portable career opportunities for military spouses.

**Who is Eligible?**

Spouses of service members on active duty in pay grades E-1 to E-9, W-1 to W-2 and O-1 to O-3 who have successfully completed high school and have the ability to request tuition assistance while their military sponsor is on Title 10 military orders are eligible.

Spouses married to members of the National Guard and reserves in these same pay grades are eligible.

Learn more about opportunities by visiting the [My Career Advancement Account](https://mycaa.militaryonesource.mil/mycaa/) website.

## Managing Stress
Pursuing higher learning can be challenging. If you need someone to talk and to listen, we are here to help.

Community Counseling can help you manage stress, balance personal challenges, and improve overall well-being, enabling you to focus on your educational goals and academic success.

Life Skills Development:

Learn more about [Community Counseling](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling)'s services and support.

## Libraries
Fostering opportunities for connection and providing access to knowledge, innovation, and creativity.

We provide access to study materials, research databases, test prep resources, and quiet study spaces, helping Marines succeed in their academic pursuits.

Life Skills Development Resources:

- Computer and Internet Access
- Live, Personalized, 24/7, World-wide Turtoring
- Quiet Study Areas
- Study Resources
- Test Prep Materials
- Virtual Library

Visit your local [library](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/libraries) or the virtual library at [DoD MWR Libraries](https://www.dodmwrlibraries.org/).

## Family Member Employment Assistance Program
Supporting military spouses and dependent family members with career readiness tools, resources, and services.

The Family Member Employment Assistance Program (FMEAP) supports your Voluntary Education by offering career counseling, job search assistance, and access to educational resources, helping you develop skills, pursue certifications, and advance your career alongside your educational goals.

Life Skills Development Resources:

- Military Spouse Education & Career Opportunities (MySECO)
- My Career Advancement Account Scholarship Program (MyCAA)
- Military Spouse Employment Partnership (MSEP)
- Military Spouse Licensure Reimbursement (MSLR)
- Transferring Your Professional License
- Spouse's Transition Readiness Seminar (S.T.A.R.S)

Learn more about the services and support available at [FMEAP](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/family-member-employment-assistance-program).

## Marine For Life Network
Building connections for transitioning Marines and family members to help them successfully reach their career goals.

The Marine For Life Network (M4LN) connects you to valuable educational resources, networking opportunities, and mentorship. It helps you navigate your educational paths, access scholarships, and prepare for career transitions, ensuring you have the support needed to succeed both academically and professionally.

Life Skills Development Resources:

- Networking
- Career Planning
- Job Searching
- Communication Skills
- Leadership Development
- Problem Solving

Grow your network through [M4LN](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/transition-readiness-program/marine-for-life-network).

## SkillBridge
Developing hands-on experience with an industry partner to gain practical skills and enhance your career potential.

SkillBridge is available to all eligible service members. All courses are geared toward learning high-demand industry-specific skills with the high probability of securing employment prior to exiting the military. Courses offer job interviews, placements, or certifications to enhance entry into the workforce.

Visit your local [SkillBridge](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/transition-readiness-program/skillbridge) and learn more about opportunities, services, and support.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Find information and get quick answers to common questions.

**What is Voluntary Education?**

Voluntary Education provides access to educational resources, counseling, and financial support to pursue higher education, certifications, and professional development.

**What types of degrees or certifications can I pursue?**

The program supports a variety of educational goals, including associates, bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees, as well as certifications and vocational training in various fields.

**Can I use my GI Bill benefits with the Voluntary Education Program?**

Yes, Marines can use their GI Bill benefits in combination with the Voluntary Education Program to help cover the cost of tuition, books, and other educational expenses.

**How do I transfer my GI Bill benefits to my dependents?**

To transfer Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits to dependents, you must meet specific eligibility requirements and apply through the Department of Defense's online platform, typically after completing at least six years of service. Visit the Education Center for more information.

**How does the Joint Service Transcripts (JST) work?**

The JST captures military training and occupation experience, which may be eligible for civilian academic credits. You can request your JST online, and it is typically sent to the college or university of your choice.

**Is there a limit to how much Tuition Assistance I can receive?**

Yes, TA typically covers up to $250 per semester, with an annual cap of $4,500 per fiscal year for eligible Marines.

**Where can I go to take the SAT/ACT?**

The Education Centers are not authorized to offer either exam. For the SAT or ACT, register and create an account with the [College Board](https://mysat.collegeboard.org/login) or [ACT.org](https://www.act.org/).

**Is military testing offered through the Education Center?**

Yes. Official military testing is offered through the Education Center and service members can test for the ASVAB, DLPT, and other professional exams.

pages.text:
# Volunteer Opportunities

We connect you with meaningful volunteering opportunities that strengthen the military community and enhance the well-being of Marines and their families.

## Now Accepting 2026 Volunteer of the Year Nominations
The office of the Commanding General MCI-West Camp Pendleton will present the winner in each category with an award at the Volunteer Recognition Ceremony held on April 23, 2026.

**REQUIREMENTS**

- Volunteer service must have been performed between January 1, 2025 - December 31, 2025.
- **Service Members:** Must be attached to a unit on base.
- **Service Members and Units:** May use volunteer service done on and off base.
- **Dependents, DoD Employees, or Civilians:** Your volunteer service must have been done on base.
- **Non-Federal Entities/Organizations:** Your service must have been to the Camp Pendleton community.

**HOW TO APPLY**

Download the Volunteer of the Year Nomination form. Follow the instructions on the form.

**DEADLINE**

March 13, 2026.

**CONTACT**

Volunteer Program
BLDG 13150
Camp Pendleton, CA
cpenvolunteer@usmc-mccs.org

## Start Volunteering Today
Make a difference by giving your time, sharing your skills, and supporting the community.

## Eligibility
Eligibility to volunteer in your community typically includes a willingness to contribute your time and skills, but specific requirements may vary by organization.

**Requirements:**

- Must be 13 years of age or older.
- Minors must have parental permission to volunteer.
- Must be willingly to offer, be accepted, and provide voluntary services.
- Must be in an off-duty status, if active duty or a civilian employee.
- Cannot count any fundraising activity as volunteerism.

## Getting Started
Getting started with volunteering is easy! Begin by identifying your interests and skills, then explore local organizations or programs that align with your passions. Reach out to volunteer coordinators for information on opportunities, and don't hesitate to ask questions to find the best fit for you. Your journey to making a difference starts today!

**Explore Volunteer Opportunities**

- Browse the volunteer webpage and calendar for available volunteer roles that match your interests and skills.

**Connect with the Volunteer Office**

- Contact the Volunteer Coordinator for more information about specific opportunities and application processes.

**Complete a Volunteer Application**

- Fill out the volunteer application form, providing necessary details such as your availability, interests, and any prior experience.

**Orientation or Training Session**

- Attend the required orientation or training to familiarize yourself with the program, expectations, and guidelines. Orientation and training may not be available at all locations.

**Complete Background Check (if applicable)**

- For certain roles, especially those working with children or sensitive information, a background check may be required.

**Get Assigned**

- After your application is approved, you'll be matched with a volunteer position that suits your skills and interests.

**Begin Volunteering!**

- Start your volunteer journey, making a positive impact on your community while gaining valuable experience.

Volunteer opportunities are available at each installation and also through Single Marine Program, L.I.N.K.S., MCFTB and more. Contact your volunteer coordinator for more information about how you can support your military community.

## Why Volunteer?
Volunteering offers many benefits, from personal growth and skill development to making meaningful connections and giving back to the community. It's a rewarding way to build new experiences, boost your resume, and create a lasting positive impact on those around you.

**Volunteering Benefits:**

- Community support
- Develop lasting relationships
- Enhances resumes
- Grow networks
- Personal growth and development
- Professional development
- Receive on-the-job training
- Teen volunteer opportunities
- Work flexible hours

**Life Skills Developed:**

- Communication
- Empathy and Compassion
- Strengthening Relationships
- Leadership
- Personal and professional development
- Problem-solving
- Networking
- Teamwork
- Time management

**Honorable Recognition:**

- Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal (MOVSM)
- President's Volunteer Service Award (PVSA)
- Volunteer Service Award (VSA)

## Volunteer Opportunities
Discover resources in your community.

## L.I.N.K.S
Lifestyle Insights, Networking, Knowledge, and Skills

**Curriculum Includes:**

- Our Corps, Our Culture
- Events & Etiquette
- Navigating Resources
- Pay & Entitlements
- Deployments
- Safe and Sound All Around
- The Place You Will Go
- Building Your Network
- Investing in Your Community
- Kids Readiness
- Mentor Training

**Volunteer!**

Are you wanting to make a difference in the lives of military families? Become a L.I.N.K.S. volunteer! Share your experience, provide valuable resources, and help fellow Marines and their families thrive in their military journey. Join us to foster community, build connections, and empower others.

Sign up today!

Learn more about L.I.N.K.S. by visiting [Marine Corps Family Team Building](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/marine-corps-family-team-building).

## Single Marine Program
Volunteering with the Single Marine Program (SMP) supports the community, events, and helps enhance the quality of life for Marines and their families.

The Single Marine Program offers a wide variety of volunteer opportunities each month with flexible times, days, and locations to meet the needs of our diverse community. Whether you're passionate about giving back through local food banks or shelters, love working with animals, or just want to get out of the barracks and have fun doing something meaningful, SMP has the perfect opportunity for you!

Volunteer opportunities are available for single and geo-bachelor Marines.

Learn more about the volunteering opportunities through the [Single Marine Program](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/single-marine-program).

## Marine Corps Family Team Building
Volunteering with Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB) empowers and supports Marine families through workshops, events, and vital resources that strengthen resilience and readiness.

**L.I.N.K.S. Volunteers**

If you are interested in becoming part of the L.I.N.K.S. team, call us or visit our office for more information. Join our dynamic group of volunteers today!

- Host/Greet at Sessions
- Food Angel – Help to Feed our Participants.
- Administrative Support
- Present L.I.N.K.S. Session Topics
- Information Booth Support
- Event Support

**UPFRP Volunteers**

Connect with your DRC or URC and discover volunteer opportunities through Marine Corps Family Team Building.

## Coach Youth Sports
Volunteering for youth sports is a fantastic way to inspire young athletes while fostering teamwork, discipline, and a love for physical activity. By supporting the community through these programs, you can make a positive impact in their lives, promote healthy habits, and create lasting memories through fun and engaging sports experiences!

- Tee-Ball
- Baseball
- Basketball
- Flag Football
- Soccer
- Track

Not all sports listed are available at all locations.
Explore volunteer opportunities with [Youth Sports](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/recreation-fitness/recreation/sports/youth-sports).

## Base Schools
Marines and their families have valuable opportunities to volunteer at schools located on Marine Corps bases, contributing positively to the educational environment and fostering community engagement.

Here's how you can get involved:

**Explore Volunteer Opportunities**

There are a variety of volunteer opportunities that connect military personnel, their families, retirees, veterans, and civilians with local schools. These programs are designed to empower individuals to share their time and talents in support of the military community.

**Benefits of Volunteering**

Volunteering provides numerous advantages, including:

- Personal Growth: Develop new skills and gain experiences that can enhance personal and professional growth.
- Community Connection: Strengthen ties within the military community by supporting local schools and educational programs.
- Recognition: Eligible volunteers may receive awards such as the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Award or the President's Volunteer Service Award.

**Volunteer Roles**

Volunteer roles in base schools can vary but often include:

- Classroom Assistance: Supporting teachers with instructional activities and classroom management.
- Tutoring: Providing one-on-one or small group academic support to students.
- Extracurricular Activities: Assisting with clubs, sports, and other after-school programs.

**Initiate the Application Process**

To begin volunteering:

- Contact the Volunteer Coordinator: Reach out to the Installation Volunteer Coordinator at your base to express interest and learn about available opportunities.
- Complete Necessary Forms: Fill out the required volunteer application forms, which may include background checks and other necessary documentation.

**Commit to a Schedule**

- Determine a volunteer schedule that aligns with your availability and the needs of the school. Consistency is often appreciated, but many programs offer flexibility to accommodate varying schedules.

**Maintain Communication**

- Stay in regular contact with the school's volunteer coordinator to ensure a positive and effective volunteer experience.

Not all installations offer volunteer opportunities with base schools. For volunteering opportunities reach out to the Volunteer Coordinator.

## Navy Marine Corps Relief Society
The Navy Marine Corps Relief Society (NMCRS) is accepting professional volunteers to assist service members and eligible family members.

**Volunteer requirements:**

- Must have base access
- Be available between Monday through Friday from 8 a.m.-4 p.m.

**Volunteer opportunities include:**

- Client services - reception duties
- Casework - providing one-on-one financial education and assistance
- Budget for Baby - teaching workshops to military families expecting a child
- Well Baby Clinic - working with our visiting nurses to administer health checks and clothing exchange

All volunteers will be properly trained to support and assist with confidence.

Learn more about volunteer opportunities at the [Navy Marine Corps Relief Society](https://www.nmcrs.org/).

## Honoring Our Volunteers
We honor the outstanding commitment to volunteer service.

## Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal
The Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal is for members of the armed forces and reserve components. Service members will want to volunteer in their civilian and military communities for normally a period of three years, which do not need to be consecutive years. The volunteering should be significant, tangible, sustained, and of a direct nature.

Learn more about the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal by contacting the Volunteer Coordinator.

## Behind the Camouflage Spouse and Community Awards
The Marine Corps Association is excited to announce the launch of the **Behind the Camouflage Awards Program** to highlight the exceptional work Marine Corps spouses and community members are doing within their communities.

There are three opportunities to nominate spouses and community members who contributed to building the community and driving positive change.

**Spouse Spotlight**

Celebrating Marine Corps Spouses who excel in building community and driving positive change. Do you know an amazing Marine Corps Spouse who is an everyday hero working tirelessly behind the scenes to improve our community?

Nominate a spouse today at [Spouse Spotlight](https://www.mca-marines.org/btc-spouse-spotlight/)!

**Changemaker**

The Changemaker of the Year Award honors individuals who have made a significant, tangible impact within the Marine Corps community. This award recognizes those who have driven meaningful change by identifying challenges and implementing solutions that positively affect the lives of Marine Corps families, spouses, and the broader community. The recipients of this award are innovators, problem-solvers, and leaders who leave a lasting legacy of improvement and progress.

Learn about eligibility and requirements, and nomination process at [Changemaker](https://www.mca-marines.org/community-change-maker/).

**Community Catalyst**

The Community Catalyst of the Year Award recognizes a member of the Marine Corps community who has shown exceptional dedication to building and nurturing a supportive environment. This award celebrates individuals who go above and beyond to create inclusive, welcoming spaces that foster connections, collaboration, and mutual support among Marine Corps families. The recipient of this award demonstrates leadership and initiative in enhancing the quality of life for those within the Marine Corps community.

Learn about eligibility, requirements, and nomination process at [Community Catalyst](https://www.mca-marines.org/community-catalyst/).

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Quick answers to common questions.

**How do I sign up to volunteer?**

You can sign up by visiting the Volunteer office, contacting a volunteer coordinator, or checking the MCCS website for available opportunities and application instructions.

**What types of volunteer opportunities are available?**

MCCS offers a wide range of opportunities, including roles in youth sports, the Single Marine Program, special events, and community support.

**Do I need prior experience or training to volunteer?**

While some positions may require specific skills or training, many volunteer opportunities offer on-the-job training and welcome individuals of all experience levels.

**How do I track my volunteer hours?**

Volunteer hours are typically tracked through sign-in sheets, volunteer logs, with verification by a coordinator or supervisor.

**Can I earn awards or recognition for my volunteer service?**

Yes, volunteers may be eligible for awards such as the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal, the President's Volunteer Service Award, and other local or organizational recognition.

pages.text:
# Recycle

The Camp Pendleton Recycling program advances environmental stewardship to fulfill Federal and State waste diversion requirements. Community participation supports quality of life improvements and preserves natural resources.

Revenue generated by the recycling initiative funds community projects including specialized wheelchairs for beaches, recreational equipment, safety materials, fitness equipment, youth sports uniforms, and transportation assets.

## Know What to Recycle
- Ammunition, Explosives & Fireworks
- Appliances (large and small)
- Autos & Automobile Products (no liquids)
- Baby Equipment
- Bicycle Tubes
- Books
- Cartons – Wood and Cardboard
- Cell Phones
- Computers, TVs & Electronics
- Cooking Oil
- Eyeglasses
- Fire Extinguishers
- Fishing Line
- Foam & Packaging Materials
- Fuel Tanks – Empty ONLY, CA Dry
- Furniture & Metal Doors
- Glass Bottles & Jars
- Hangers
- Hearing Aids
- Helium Tanks
- Ink Jet Cartridges
- Junk Mail
- Medical Equipment & Supplies
- Metal Cans
- Moving Boxes
- Pallets & Wood
- Paper Shredding
- Paper, Paperboard, Magazines, and Cardboard
- Phone Books
- Plastics
- Pots & Pans
- Propane Tanks – Empty ONLY
- Refrigerators
- Scrap Metals
- Smoke Detectors
- Sporting Goods & Equipment
- Washers and Dryers

Dispose of old medications at the Navy Hospital on base.

## The Camp Pendleton Recycling Program
Recycling reduces waste volume in base landfills and meets federal, state, and local requirements.

**Family Housing**
- All homes receive recycling bins for curbside collection
- Aluminum & metal cans, plastic & glass bottles, jugs, and jars may be commingled
- Newspaper, chipboard, cereal boxes, paper, cardboard, and junk mail go in separate containers
- Excess recyclables in clear plastic bags placed next to bins
- Trash never belongs in recycling bins
- Plastic grocery bags return to commissary or grocery store
- Contact housing office for bulky items (furniture, washers, dryers)
- Dumping trash and bulky items is illegal
- Scavenging reduces funding for community projects

**BEQ Residents**
- Locate building recycling bins or contact barracks/S-4 officer if unavailable
- Flatten cardboard boxes into white dumpsters labeled "cardboard"
- Place newspapers and paper in Blue containers labeled "paper only"
- Deposit bottles and cans in labeled containers
- Call 725-4892 if containers are full
- E-Waste and Universal Waste delivery to 13 Area or 52 Area Recycling Centers during operating hours
- 24/7 drop sites at:
  - 13 Area, BLDG 13193 (Mon-Thu 9am-2pm)
  - 22 Area, BLDG 22054 (Mon-Fri 7:30am-3pm)
  - 52 Area, BLDG 520189 (Mon-Thu 9am-2pm)
- Scavenging is illegal and reduces community funding

**Area Commanders**
- Appoint Recycling Coordinator
- Attend quarterly recycling meetings
- Select staging areas and collection points
- Request containers for identified waste streams
- Ensure Privacy Act compliance for paper recycling
- Coordinate collection dates with Recycling Manager (725-4982)

**Unit Commanders and S-4 Officers**
- Attend quarterly recycling meetings
- Identify waste streams and coordinate container needs
- Appoint collection point contacts
- Ensure Privacy Act compliance
- Enforce Base Order 6280.5B compliance

## Important Recycling Information
**Work Spaces**
- Blue 90-Gallon Bins: ONLY non-PII paper
- Brown 90-Gallon Bins: Recyclables (aluminum cans, glass drinking bottles, plastic bottles)
- Dual Metal Frames: Non-PII paper
- Items NOT in Blue 90-Gallon Bins: No PII paper, trash, aluminum cans, glass drinking bottles, or plastic bottles
- Items NOT in Brown 90-Gallon Bins: No trash, electronics, monitors, CPU, radios, TVs, LCDs, cable wires, computers, phones, laptops, vacuums, VCRs, CD players, XBox, Nintendo, electronic toys, hair dryers
- Items NOT in Plastic Racks Frames: Non-PII paper, trash, or recyclables

**Housing**
- Recycling Bins Accept: Cardboard, aluminum cans, metal cans, glass, plastic, miscellaneous plastic, shrink wrap, bubble wrap, polystyrene
- Recycling Bins DO NOT Accept: Trash, food waste, dirt, paper towels, ceramics, baby diapers, dog poop, mirrors, furniture or motor vehicles, green waste, mulch, bushes, logs
- Hazardous Materials: Paint, glass cleaner, car oil, cooking oil, car batteries, household batteries, lightbulbs, expired fuel, car tires
- Textiles: Contact thrift store by Lake O'Neill for uniforms, shoes, shirts, pants, sweaters, jackets
- Food: Place in trash containers; if in recyclable container, empty first
- Dead Animals: Contact Animal Control (760) 725-8120
- Microwaves/Refrigerators: Contact Housing Managers (hazardous materials)

**Bachelor Enlisted Quarters**
- Small Red Container Accept: Aluminum cans, glass drinking bottles, plastic bottles (and non-PII paper in separate container)
- Three-Compartment Containers: Recyclables and non-PII materials
- Small Red Containers DO NOT Accept: Trash
- Three Compartment Container DO NOT Accept: Non-PII paper, electronics, monitors, CPU, radios, TVs, LCDs, cable wires, computers, phones, laptops, vacuums, VCRs, CD players, XBox, Nintendo, electronic toys, hair dryers

**Gas Stations**
- Blue 90-Gallon Bins Accept: Aluminum cans, glass bottles, plastic bottles, non-PII paper
- Blue 90-Gallon Bins DO NOT Accept: Trash, electronics, monitors, CPUs, radios, TVs, LCDs, cable wires, computers, phones, laptops, vacuums, VCRs, CD players, XBox, Nintendo, electronic toys, hair dryers, hazardous material, paint, glass cleaner, car oil, cooking oil, car batteries, household batteries, lightbulbs, expired fuel, car tires
- Textiles: Turn in to thrift store by Lake O'Neill (shoes, shirts, pants, sweaters, jackets, uniforms)
- Food: Place in trash containers; if in recyclable container, empty first
- Dead Animals: Contact Animal Control (760) 725-8120
- Microwaves: Contact Housing Managers (refrigerators, electronics, tires considered hazardous)

## FAQs
**Where can I recycle electronic and other forms of hazardous waste?**
For usable personal property, donate to charitable organizations or off-base resellers. Lincoln & Hunt Housing residents contact their respective housing departments. Hazardous waste turn-in events occur off-base in surrounding cities. Contact Base Housing Management for procedures.

**What materials can we recycle?**
Cardboard, paper, aluminum, plastic bottles and cans, glass bottles and jars, and scrap metals. Includes detergent and shampoo bottles, metal food cans, and cereal/food boxes.

**Where can I drop off my recyclable materials?**
Drop at recycling centers in 13 Area, 22 Area, and 52 Area during operating hours. After-hours drop-off available (no electronic or household hazardous waste).

**Who do I call when I need assistance or have a question?**
Call the Base Recycling Manager at (760) 212-3934.

**Who is required to recycle at Camp Pendleton?**
Everyone. Base Order MCIWEST-MCB CAMPENO 6280.1 requires all MCB Camp Pendleton occupants to recycle.

**Can someone other than Camp Pendleton Recycling staff or Waste Management remove recyclables from bins and containers?**
No. Scavenging is illegal and should be reported to PMO or the Recycling Manager.

**Do you give money back for bottles and cans?**
No. We are not a redemption center. Revenue from recyclables sales funds the Base Recycling Program and morale, welfare, and recreation projects after overhead expenses.

**Can we use plastic bags?**
No. All bags holding recyclables must be transparent.

**I live in family housing and I need recycling bins. Who can I call?**
Contact your housing management office.

**Do I have to wash out empty bottles, jars, and cans?**
No, but recommended to reduce flies, vermin, and odors.

**Do I need to remove the label from bottles, jars, and cans?**
No. Label removal is no longer required.

**Do you accept shredded paper?**
Yes, as long as placed in clear plastic bags.

**Do you accept styrofoam?**
Yes. All packaging material accepted, especially from televisions and computers.

# Veterans Access

## Welcome to Camp Pendleton, Veterans!
Effective Jan 1, 2020, all service-connected disabled veterans, Medal of Honor & Purple Heart recipients, former prisoners of war, VA benefits eligible veterans & primary veteran caregivers will be eligible to shop at the commissary, MCCS retail stores & participate in select MCCS recreational activities.

[Do I Qualify?](https://www.pendleton.marines.mil/Staff/Principal-Staff/Security-and-Emergency-Services/Base-Access/#frequently-asked-questions)

## What is available to qualifying Veterans?

## Recreation
Recreation is critical to overall physical and mental health and participating in these activities helps manage stress, create a sense of balance and increase productivity and quality of life. Even after serving on active duty, mental and physical wellness is vital to success. Here are some of MCCS Indoor and Outdoor offerings to include golf, beaches, campgrounds, bowling and auto skills to explore.

[Recreation Info](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/recreation-fitness/recreation)

## Shopping
Camp Pendleton is home to the largest Marine Corps Exchange (MCX), conveniently located near the Main Gate across the street from Pacific Plaza and the Commissary. Enjoy a wide variety of items in over a 147,000 sq ft shopping area. The MCX offers tax-free shopping, price matching, and specials. In addition to the large MCX, Camp Pendleton also offers the Mainside Marine Mart, San Onofre MCX, and over ten fuel stations located throughout the base. All MCX offerings including fuel are tax-free!

[Shopping Info](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/shopping)

## Lodging
Come stay with us! We're home to the Pacific Views Lodge and Ward Lodge, both offering comfort for you and your family. If the outdoors is more your style, MCCS offers a variety of Camping options along with coastal lodging in our ocean front Beach Cottages.

[Lodging Info](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/lodging)

## Dining
MCCS is always working to diversify our on base eatery options offering only the best for our military community, from coffee and sandwiches to a meal on the golf course. MCCS has you covered.

[Dining Info](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/dining-entertainment/dining)

## Volunteer Programs
Still want to participate in military activities and support the active duty, then become a volunteer by visiting our Volunteer Program! We would love to have you at our events!

[Volunteer Info](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/volunteer-opportunities)

## Theater
Our recently renovated MCCS Theater features current movies for the whole family to enjoy, with affordable tickets and fresh popcorn. The theater is a great date night or weekend oasis to escape the summer heat!

[Theater Info](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/dining-entertainment/theater)

## Retiree Services
Any questions on retiree services can be answered at our Retired Activities Offices. Questions on military retired pay, VA care, referrals, and transitional employment, federal and state benefits, legal advice, consumer protection, changes to allotments, and more, our team is here to help.

[Retiree Info](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/retired-affairs)

## Catering & Events
Planning your next big event? MCCS has facilities to make the perfect venue for you and your family! Weddings, retirement parties, birthdays and more our catering and events team is ready to help.

[Catering & Events Info](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/dining-entertainment/event-planning-multimedia/event-planning)

# Welcome to Camp Pendleton

Whether you are arriving on your first assignment, transitioning with your family, or joining our community as a civilian employee, we are committed to helping make your move as smooth and successful as possible.

## Check Into Command
All Marines checking into the following are to report to the Installation Personnel Administration Center (IPAC) Inbound Center, BLDG 13107 (directly across from the 13 Area Mess Hall):

- 1st Marine Division
- 1st Marine Logistics Group
- I Marine Expeditionary Force
- Marine Aircraft Group 39
- Marine Corps Air Station
- Marine Corps Base
- Weapons and Field Training Battalion

**After-Hours Check-In Information**
A duty officer is available 24-hours a day to assist Marines reporting to Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton outside of normal working hours and to endorse required check-in documentation.

For additional information, please contact the Installation Personnel Administration Center (IPAC) Inbound Center.

## Housing Office
The Family Housing Office provides assistance whether you decide to live on or off base. If you desire to live aboard the base, you are encouraged to submit an advance application to the Family Housing Office once you receive your web orders.

With your CAC card and NMCI account you can digitally sign the Housing Application Forms located on [Camp Pendleton Family Housing](https://www.pendleton.marines.mil/Staff/Principal-Staff/G-F-Facilities/#Tab/family-housing).

Please limit the size of emails to 8MB per email. If you do not have CAC access you can download and send as an e-mail attachment or fax the application. You can also drop-off your application at the Joint Housing Office, 98 San Jacinto Road (near the main gate located off of Interstate 5).

Family Housing at MCB Camp Pendleton has been "privatized." Public-Private Venture (PPV) partners, [Lincoln Military Housing](https://livelmh.com/installations/camp-pendleton-mcb/) and [Hunt Military Communities](http://www.deluzfamilyhousing.com/) are responsible for the day-to-day management and maintenance of 7,795 homes aboard the base.

If you decide to live off base, our Housing Referral Section can assist you in relocating to a local Southern California community. Referral Section services include home purchase information, finance and refinance referrals, conventional, Cal-Vet and other loan information, and landlord/tenant mediation services.

## Installation Personnel Administration Center (IPAC)
Hours of operation for Installation Personnel Administration Center (IPAC), unless directed otherwise, are as follows:

**Inbound Branch, BLDG 13107**
Monday - Friday: 7:30am - 4:30pm

## DMO/Household Goods
The Distribution Management Office (DMO) is your primary resource for transportation and personal property support during a Permanent Change of Station (PCS) move. DMO provides guidance and assistance with household goods shipments, storage, vehicle transportation, inbound and outbound moves, and other transportation-related services for military members, civilian employees, and their families.

Our goal is to provide timely, professional, and customer-focused support to help make your transition to, from, or within Camp Pendleton as smooth as possible. Because transportation entitlements and policies may change, we encourage you to contact our office directly if you have questions regarding your specific situation.

pages.title: 24/7 Access
pages.text:
# 24/7 Access

## ACCESS & ENTRY
- **Your CAC is Your Key**
Access is for authorized patrons, 18 years and older, with a registered Common Access Card (CAC).
- **One Swipe, One Entry**
You must swipe your own CAC every single time you enter.
- **Going Solo**
Guests, contractors, and anyone without a registered CAC are strictly prohibited during unstaffed hours.
- **Never Prop the Door**
Propping or holding the door open is strictly forbidden and will result in the loss of your access privileges. Ensure the door closes fully behind you.
- **Resetting for Unstaffed Hours**
If you are in the gym when it closes and staff leaves, you must exit the building and re-enter by swiping your CAC to ensure you are accounted for.

## RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
- **You're in Charge**
You are now your own safety officer. Train smart, do not exercise beyond your limits, and avoid horseplay.
- **Stay in Your Lane**
Do not enter restricted areas like the HITT Center, saunas, front desk, or offices, even if they appear unsecured. Tampering with locks or chains is prohibited.
- **Behave Accordingly**
You are expected to conduct yourself in accordance with military rules and standards.

## EMERGENCIES & REPORTING
- **For Emergencies**
In case of an emergency, use the emergency information located near the phone at the front desk to report the issue.
- **For Facility Issues**
Report any non-emergency problems (e.g., broken equipment, burned-out lights) in the logbook at the front desk.

## VIOLATIONS & CONSEQUENCES
- **Know the Stakes**
Any violation of these rules may result in the immediate revocation of your 24/7 access privileges.
- **Report to Command**
Violations by active-duty personnel will be reported to their command for potential disciplinary action under the UCMJ. Civilian violations will be reported to the Provost Marshal's Office (PMO).
- **Stay Current**
You must sign a Statement of Understanding (SOU) for each facility you wish to use and renew it annually to maintain access.

## Resource Downloads
- [Fitness Center Facility Usage Request](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=956acbc8-1f5a-41bf-ab27-e5babf67c583&v=1)
- [Unstaffed and Hybrid Fitness Centers Policy](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=095ba8c8-8339-4f5c-9a7b-be74acb254d7&v=1)

## Parent and Child Swim Lessons
**Lesson Fees**

| | |
|---|---|
| Parent & Child (offered June-July) | $28 |

## Opportunities
For information on Lifeguard and Swim Instructor opportunities, please call (760) 725-4344.

## Swim Survival Training S3T
**Who provides the training?**
MCCS Aquatics Coaches who are specifically trained in the program components.

**Do I have to take the entire class?**
Yes, but through discussion with the instructor, accommodations can be made on a case-by-case basis.

**Will equipment be provided?**
We are currently exploring avenues to fund equipment and will hopefully be able to provide the proper equipment in the future. Blouse and trousers will, however, be required.

**Will the class schedule be flexible?**
Yes, we will try to be as accommodating as possible. Classes are 1 hour long (estimated).

**Can I take the Swim Survival Skills Training (S3T) to prepare for any aquatic school?**
Yes, if you find the class helpful for your specific training, Swim Survival Skills Training (S3T) is designed to increase aquatic stamina.

**If I am in the Navy, can I take the Swim Survival Skills Training (S3T)?**
Yes. Swim Survival Skills Training (S3T) is available for all active duty, but is designed for Marine Corps Swim Qualifications.

**Can I take the Swim Survival Skills Training (S3T) if I am not going for swim qualification?**
Yes, classes are designed to help teach active duty personnel better swimming mechanics in general as well as the swim qualification.

**Can I do bottom samples and underwater crossovers with this training?**
No, that is specific training where a Marine Corps Instructor of Water Survival (MCIWS) is required to be present.

**How do I schedule a class?**
Call the 13 Area Pool to schedule (760) 725-4344.

## Rules
**Admittance**
- An I.D. card is required for admittance to the pool facility.
- An adult must accompany children under the age of 10 at all times. Children under the age of 10 will not be left at the pool facility without an adult.

**General Rules**

Reference: NAVMED P-5010-4, MCCS 1700.39

- All patrons must comply with the directions and signals of Lifeguards and/or Lifeguard Supervisor.
- Patrons must take a cleansing shower prior to entering the pool.
- No persons with sores, skin diseases, or bandages will be permitted in the pool.
- Spitting, urinating, or otherwise contaminating the pool or walkways is prohibited.
- Eating or drinking within the pool facility is permitted in designated areas only.
- Glass in any form will not be permitted at the pool facility.
- Smoking or Vaping in the pool or on the pool deck is prohibited.
- No pets are allowed in pool area. (A guide dog escorting a blind person will be permitted on the pool deck and in restrooms. Also, working dogs accompanied by handlers will be permitted in swimming pool area as required.)
- Boisterous or rough play is not permitted in the pool area.
- Non-swimmers are permitted in shallow area only.
- Diving is permitted in designated areas only.
- No fraternizing with Lifeguards.
- Climbing on Lifeguard towers or using lifesaving equipment for other than emergency use is strictly prohibited.
- Emergency Procedures: When emergency procedures are implemented, swimmers must exit the pool immediately upon signal or request by the lifeguard.
- Pool toys are provided by the facility, any additional toys are subject to approval by pool management.
- Rafts, air mattresses, noodle, or flotation devices that could easily become detached from the user are prohibited during recreation swim. United States Coast Guard approved lifejackets, floatation belts, and etc. are authorized in the shallow end only.
- Kickboards and other like items shall only be used for lap swimming, fitness training, and swim instruction.
- Breath-holding or the practice of hyperventilation is strictly prohibited while in the pool.
- Proper swimming attire only. Boots and full combat load will not be permitted.
- No tanning oils permitted.
- Marine Combat Instruction of Water Safety, Unit Training will be referred to 43, 62, or 51 Area Pools due to lack of capability, instructors, and safety structure. Unit training and the combat uniform with full combat load will not be permitted.

**Items Not Allowed in the Pool Area**
- Alcoholic beverages
- Infant walkers, glass containers, pets, and any other item deemed unsafe by the lifeguards
- No radios other than a device that may be connected to headphones will be allowed in the facility.
- Built-in floatation devices within swimsuits, water wings, noodles, and innertubes will not be permitted. Only Coast Guard-approved life vests will be allowed.
- No weight belts allowed in the pool
- Snorkels will not be permitted for recreation swim.
- No hard or inflexible toys (i.e. torpedoes, regulation football, plastic frisbees) will be allowed in the facility.

# Auto Skills

The Auto Skills Center offers an extensive collection of tools, advanced machinery, battery chargers, a brake center, steam cleaners, and electronic testing equipment to help support auto needs. There is plenty of stall space to work on vehicles, and knowledgeable mechanics are on-hand for advice and assistance. The Auto Skills Center is your source for everything your vehicle may need on Camp Pendleton!

Do it all yourself with ASE Certified expert advice at every step.

- Affordable Auto Parts Shop with everything from oil to brakes to lights
- Extensive tool collection and a wide range of machinery services
- Stall rentals for a clean and safe workspace
- On-site, expert support from knowledgeable mechanics

## Pricing
**Auto Stalls**
- Flat: $7.75/hour
- Lift: $12.75/hour
- Motorcycle Lift: $7.50/hour
- Overnight Stall Rate: $10/day

**On-Board Computer Check**
$30 (Free retesting)

**Charging System Test**
$10

$10 (30 minutes)

**Vacuum Leak Tester**
$25

- Light Truck: $15

**Machine Shop Services**
- Brake Drum Resurface: $20/each
- Brake Rotor Resurface: $20/each
- Engine Oil Drain Retreating: $25/each
- Hydraulic Press Work: $50/hour (1hr minimum)
- Service Struts: $35/each
- Vacuum Leak Test: $30/each

Fees for other machine shop tasks are determined by the amount of work required to perform the task. Check with a manager for pricing and availability.

**Welding / Fabrication**
- 110V MIG Welder, Certified Staff (30 minutes): $25
- 220V MIG Welder, Certified Staff (30 minutes): $35
- Oxy Acetylene, Certified Staff (30 minutes): $25
- 110V MIG Welder, Patron (30 minutes): $20
- 220V MIG Welder, Patron (30 minutes): $30
- Oxy Acetylene, Patron (30 minutes): $25

## Policy & Rules
- Stall issuance, machine shop, and tire services are secured 90 minutes before the posted closing time. Customer cleanup starts 45 minutes before close!
- 30-day temporary storage for vehicles being worked on Auto Skills Center ($20.00/day)
- Recycle Center for waste, antifreeze, automotive oils, batteries, and old auto parts/scrap metal (**we will only take parts that are adequately drained of all fluids; please drain them before dropping them off at our facility**).
- Vehicle code scanner and all data is available
- Alternator, battery, and starter available
- Hand tools available within the facility

**Have a project? We have long-term stall discounts available.**

Enjoy a 60% or more discount when you take advantage of these great deals! The regular flat stall fee is $7.50 per hour/$60 per day plus the overnight price of $15 total per day, $75. Two weeks on an hourly contract totals $750, and 1 month $1500. Thus, see the two options below that will save you money that you can use towards your project.

15- and 30-consecutive days options to choose from:

**Option 1 - 15 consecutive days**
For $250, rent a long-term stall for 15 consecutive days
Included are 2 hours of lift and 30 minutes of power wash use.

- This fee must be prepaid and is nonrefundable; no transferring of stalls or substituting of vehicles.
- The lift and power wash allowance must be used within 15 days; this incentive expires after 15 days and can only be used for the vehicle assigned to the long-term stall.

**Option 2 - 30 consecutive days**
For $400, rent a long-term stall for 30 consecutive days. Included are 4 hours of lift and 1 hour of power wash use.

- This fee must be prepaid and is nonrefundable; no transferring of stalls or substituting of vehicles.
- Lift and power wash must be used within 30 days; this incentive expires after 30 days and can only be used for the vehicle assigned to the long-term stall.

**Temporary Storage (outdoors)**
$15/day

To utilize the Auto Skills Center, you must meet eligibility and ownership requirements. The following will need to be proved: a DoD ID card (CAC, Retired, reserve, or dependent ID) along with the vehicle registration or proof of insurance in the patron's name upon check-in. (Please bring these items to the check-in window to utilize the Auto Skills Center) Please Note: DoD contractors are not eligible.

- Our shop services are secured 90 minutes before the posted closing time (machine shop, tire services)
- Stall issuance will secure 90 minutes before the posted closing time.
- Stall cleanup will commence 45 minutes before the posted closing time.
- Auto Skills Center tools are not allowed to leave the premises.
- Please follow all directions the Auto Skills Staff provided about Safety and Hazardous Waste. If unsure, please ask any Auto Skills staff for assistance.
- Closed-toe shoes are **required** when inside the Auto Skills compound (sandals or open-toe shoes are not allowed).
- For safety reasons: No children under 13 years old are allowed in the work area. A customer waiting area is available if necessary.
- No unsupervised children are allowed at the Auto Skills Center.
- Smoking is not allowed within the Auto Skills Center. (This includes e-cigarettes or other vaping products). There is a designated smoking area located in our parking lot if necessary.
- No consumption of alcoholic beverages is allowed in the Auto Skills compound.
- No personal welding/torch equipment is allowed at the Auto Skills Center.
- No personal paint equipment (paint guns or airless paint equipment) is allowed within the Auto Skills Center.
- No pets are allowed within the Auto Skills Center compound (exception: service animals).

## Suppliers & Brands
Our objective is to support a shopping experience for Marines, having access to needed and elective automotive parts, accessories, and products. Full access to the vendors below will allow service members, retirees, DoD personnel, veterans, and family members to repair, service, and perform upgrades in the comfort and confidence of their MCB Auto Skills Center.

**Highline Warren**
Highline Warren is North America's premier distributor of automotive chemicals and products.

**Factory Motor Parts**
OEM parts provider with a vast inventory available for next-day delivery. Repair & service parts, batteries, and complete engines.

**NAPA**
A trusted source for automotive parts, accessories & know-how for your car, truck, or SUV.

**O'Reilly Automotive**
An American auto parts retailer that provides automotive aftermarket parts, tools, supplies, equipment, and accessories to professional service providers and do-it-yourself customers.

Variety of brands include:

- AMSOIL
- Royal Purple
- Red Line
- Mobil 1
- Lucas
- Motorcraft

## Need tires?
At MCCS Auto Skills Center, we've got your tire needs covered. Whether you're seeking performance, durability, or a smooth ride, we offer a diverse range of tires from renowned brands, all at a special Military discounted price.

**Ways to order:**

- Call us to get a quote over the phone at (760) 725-5092 or
- Stop by our Retail Store and utilize our tire kiosk to compare brands and prices. Our knowledgeable staff is ready to assist you in finding the perfect match based on tire size, vehicle type, or SKU #.

The Auto Skills Center offers installation for only $24.99 per tire when you purchase a tire from our facility. Installation includes dismount, mount, balancing, and disposal. Take advantage of the a tax-free purchase and other local fees waived.

## Window Tinting
Need your windows tinting? Give us a call! Or call Solar Care directly at (760) 519-4294 and set up an appointment to get your windows tinted here at Auto Skills. These services are mobile and provided anywhere on Camp Pendleton. Please mention Auto Skills when you call them.

**Offered Services:**
