pages.title: Marina
pages.text:
# Marina

The Del Mar Marina provides a variety of services including sailing courses, boat rentals, clinics, offshore cruises, slips, and dry storage.

Services include:

- Sailing and Power Boat Rentals
- Kayak, Stand-Up, and Pedal Boat Rentals
- Adult and Youth Sailing Courses
- Slips and Dry Storage (for privately owned boats)
- Special Events

Open on Federal Holidays May-Sep.

## Lessons & Course Overview
**Learn to Sail and Explore the Coast**

The progression begins with the Learn to Sail course, taught in the protected boat basin where students can build foundational skills in a safe and fun setting. Located just 10 minutes from the ocean, the training area provides an ideal transition to real-world sailing conditions.

After completing Learn to Sail, students can advance to Basic Keelboat, a US Sailing certified course, where they gain the skills needed to sail independently on the ocean.

Additional courses help sailors prepare for more advanced adventures:
- **Seamanship Course**: Develop the confidence and practical skills needed for coastal cruising.
- **Navigation Course**: Learn the art of traditional chart navigation and deepen your understanding of coastal passage planning.

**Specialty Clinics**

Throughout the year, clinics are offered including: Spinnaker Handling, Engine Maintenance, Celestial Navigation, and Bareboat Chartering.

After completing each course, participants are eligible to independently rent the boats they trained on.

## Learn to Sail Course
**Prerequisite:** None.

**Duration:** 3 days (usually over two weekends)

The Learn to Sail Course is designed for individuals with little or no sailing experience. Classes are offered every month on weekends. Students learn essential sailing fundamentals, including: Boat safety, Rigging and boat preparation, How sails work, Points of sail, Basic knots, Sail trim, Sailing terminology and nomenclature, Rules of the road, and Fundamental sailing techniques.

Participants get out on the water on the very first day of class. Instruction takes place aboard a Capri 16.5 sailboat equipped with a mainsail and jib. The course fee includes the Learn Sailing Right textbook, and students are encouraged to take advantage of complimentary practice sailing sessions before the final day of instruction.

**Important Information:** Please note that sailing these boats requires moderate physical movement, including shifting from one side of the boat to the other while underway. Individuals with knee, back, or mobility concerns are encouraged to contact the sailing center before registering.

**Course Fee:** $300/participant includes the Learn Sailing Right textbook

## Basic Keelboat Course
**Prerequisite:** Completion of the Learn to Sail Course or successful challenge of the program prior to the course start date.

**Duration:** 3 days (over two weekends)

After mastering the fundamentals of sailing, it's time to take your skills to the next level and venture into the open ocean. The Basic Keelboat Course introduces sailors to coastal sailing and cruising along the Southern California coastline, where encounters with dolphins, sea lions, and even whales are common.

Students will head out to sea on the very first day of class and gain practical experience in: sail trim and sail handling, anchoring techniques, VHF radio operations, reefing procedures, outboard motor operation, docking and maneuvering, crew-overboard recovery, weather awareness and forecasting, basic chart reading and navigation, and coastal cruising skills.

Instruction is conducted aboard a Catalina 22 sailboat and combines classroom learning with extensive on-the-water training.

**Course Materials & Benefits**
- Included with registration: US Sailing Basic Keelboat textbook, US Sailing Logbook, and a one-year membership with US Sailing.
- Upon successful completion, participants receive: US Sailing Keelboat Certification, United States Naval Sailing Association Qualification B Skipper, qualification to rent Catalina 22 sailboats for day sailing, and eligibility to participate in fleet cruises, including trips to Dana Point, Mission bay and Catalina

**Course Fee:** $375/participant includes all course materials and books

## Advanced Seamanship Course
**Prerequisite:** Completion of the Keelboat/Cruising Course and a minimum of 16 hours logged as Skipper on the ocean.

**Duration:** 2-day weekend course

The Seamanship Course is designed for sailors who are ready to refine their skills, build confidence, and become more capable coastal cruisers. This intensive weekend program focuses on practical seamanship techniques and advanced boat-handling skills. Topics covered include: charting, navigation, set and drift, GPS operation, mooring procedures, advanced sail trim, anchoring techniques, docking and maneuvering, crew-overboard (COB) recovery, reefing and heavy-weather preparation, and additional seamanship and boat-handling skills.

Training is conducted aboard the club's Catalina 27 sailboats, providing valuable experience on larger cruising vessels. Qualification on the Catalina 27 is not required prior to enrollment.

**Recommended Materials**
- Participants will be provided: NOAA Chart 18740
- The following navigation tools will be provided for in class use: parallel rulers or navigation plotter, dividers, pencils, eraser, navigation calculator (optional)

**Course Benefits:** By the end of the weekend, participants will have improved their confidence, boat-handling abilities, and decision-making skills while gaining practical experience that supports more advanced coastal cruising and future sailing qualifications.

**Fee:** $200/participant includes all course materials and charts

## Youth Discover Sailing & Kayaking
**Ages:** 8-17 years.

**Schedule:** June - August, Wednesday - Friday: 9am - 4:30pm

**Duration:** 3 days

Welcome to the Youth Discover Sailing & Kayaking Course! This exciting hands-on program introduces young adventurers to the fundamentals of sailing and kayaking in a safe, fun, and supportive environment.

**Course Highlights:** Students will sail aboard Expo 16.5 sailboats, spend one morning learning kayaking skills on sit-on-top kayaks, and also learn how to operate a paddleboard. Classes are conducted in protected waters and combine classroom instruction with extensive hands-on practice.

Participants will be out on the water on the very first day and will learn: basic boat handling and skipper skills, basic knots, boat safety, capsize awareness and recovery concepts, how sails work, points of sail, responsibility on and around the boat, rigging and boat preparation, sail trim, sailing terminology and nomenclature, teamwork.

**What To Bring**
- **Footwear**: Closed-toe shoes are required at all times. Tennis shoes work well, provided they do not have black soles. Reef walkers or old tennis shoes are recommended for kayaking activities on Thursday.
- **Clothing**: swimsuit (the kids like to get wet every day), change of clothes, towel, sweatshirt or light jacket
- **Sun Protection**: hat, sunscreen (SPF 30+), sunglasses with a retaining strap
- **Other Essentials**: Refillable water bottle, lunch, and snacks; a soda machine is available onsite. Participants also have access to a refrigerator, microwave, and water cooler for refilling water bottles.

**Important Information:** Please arrive on time each day. The course covers a significant amount of information and hands-on instruction, and punctuality helps students get the most from their experience.

**Course Benefits:** By the end of the program, participants will have gained basic sailing and kayaking skills, increased confidence and independence, team-building and communication skills, a greater sense of responsibility, and an appreciation for boating safety and outdoor recreation.

**Course Fee:** $200/participant. Advance reservations are required.

## Regattas & Cruises
**Seasonal Sailing Regattas**

Throughout the year, sailors have the opportunity to test their skills and enjoy friendly competition during our three annual regattas, held in the Spring, Fall, and Winter. Open to sailors ages 10 and older who are qualified to rent a Capri 16.5, these events offer a fun way to gain experience and improve sailing techniques.

Participants will compete in as many races as conditions and time allow, providing opportunities to practice: racing tactics and strategy, sail trim and boat speed, starting procedures, boat handling skills, decision-making under pressure, sportsmanship and teamwork. At the conclusion of racing, awards will be presented to top performers.

**Boat Requirements:** Requires a skipper and crew member. Crew must be capable of operating the jib and handling jib sheets.

**Registration Fee:** $30/boat

Please check the sailing center calendar for upcoming regatta dates and registration information. Sailors interested in improving their racing skills are also encouraged to attend the Race Clinic.

**Overnight Sailing Cruises**

Take your sailing adventures beyond the harbor and join us for one of our exciting Overnight Sailing Cruises. These popular trips provide the perfect opportunity to build cruising experience, explore new destinations, and enjoy unforgettable weekends on the water with fellow sailors.

Throughout the year, overnight cruises are organized to Southern California destinations, including: Dana Point, Glorietta Bay, Mission Bay, and Catalina Island.

**Why Join an Overnight Cruise?**
- Gain practical coastal cruising experience
- Improve navigation and seamanship skills
- Build confidence in varying sailing conditions
- Explore new ports and destinations
- Meet and sail with fellow boating enthusiasts
- Enjoy a fun-filled weekend away from home

**Upcoming Cruises:** Cruise destinations and schedules vary throughout the year, and new trips are added regularly based on member interest and seasonal opportunities. For current schedules, availability, and registration information, please stop by the office or contact us directly.

## Marina Rules
- Renters must be a qualified patron and in possession of a current DOD ID.
- All boats must be signed out by an adult 18 years or older (that is an authorized patron).
- Operators of power vessels shall be at least 18 years of age.
- Must wear Personal Flotation Devices on all vessels at **all times**. Children 12 years and younger and non-swimmers must wear PFDs on the docks. Exception on the Duffy: Only those under the age of 13 and don't know how to swim are required to wear a PFD.
- No children under the weight of 15 lbs allowed on any MCCS vessels.
- Skippers must be licensed, fill out manifest, and are fully responsible for vessel and crew.
- Skipper must ensure compliance with all state and federal regulations.
- Report all accidents or injuries to Marina staff.
- Alcohol and boats don't mix; intoxication is prohibited on any MCCS boat.
- No rental boats out of harbor in heavy weather or small craft advisories.
- Capsized or Disabled Boat – STAY WITH THE BOAT.
- No picking up additional passengers not listed on the manifest.
- No sailing into slips unless motor problems. Please call marina for assistance.
- Skipper is responsible for leaving the vessel clean inside and out after use.
- No black-soled shoes or high heels; wear proper boating shoes.
- No pets on rental boats or equipment.
- Military vessels have right of way in basin and channel.
- No beaching of boats. Exception: kayaks without pedals
- Porta-potties must be cleaned thoroughly after use. Skipper is responsible.
- Fishing is allowed on all boats. Exception: Duffy, Capri's, Expo

**Boat Capacities**
- Paddle Boards (SUP): 1 person; basin and harbor only
- Kayaks: 1-2 persons; basin and harbor only
- Pedal Boats: 1-4 persons; basin only
- 12.5 Expo: 1-2 persons; basin and harbor only
- 16.5′ Capri: 1-4 persons; basin and harbor only
- 13.5′ Power Boat: 1-4 persons (max 650lbs); basin and harbor only
- 18' Duffy: 1-9 persons (max 1500lbs); basin and harbor only
- 22′ Catalina: 2-5 persons; see staff for boundary limits
- 25′-27′ Catalina: 2-6 persons; see staff for boundary limits
- 30′ Newport: 2-6 persons; see staff for boundary limits

**No single-handed sailing of 22′ and above** (Crew member must be at least 16 years old)

- Skipper's card remains the property of MCCS and may be revoked for careless or negligent use of equipment, failure to properly unrig and clean boat, violation or disregard of safe boating practices and failure to obey all rules and regulations. IF IN DOUBT – ASK!!
- Sailboats 22' and above are the only vessels allowed in open ocean.
- Pedal boats are restricted to the Del Mar basin only; all other vessels are restricted to the harbor.

**SPEED IN THE BASIN, CHANNEL, AND OCEANSIDE HARBOR IS NO WAKE.**

**Paddle Boards (SUP):** Anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by, and under the direct supervision of an individual at least 18 years old. All boards are restricted to the harbors. Beaching of the boards is prohibited (due to fins).

**Kayaks:** Anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by, and under the direct supervision of an individual at least 18 years old. All kayaks are restricted to the harbors. Beaching of the Hobie (pedal) kayak is prohibited due to under water fins.

**Pedal Boats:** Anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by, and under the direct supervision of an individual at least 18 years old. All pedal boats are restricted to the boat basin.

**Sailboat Qualifications:** All sailboat skippers must have a Certification Card from Camp Pendleton and must be qualified in the boat they are renting.

**Sailing Card Other Facility:** Holders of sailing qualifications from other sailing facilities will be recognized on comparable boats if proof can be provided of their sailing experience (log books). A full practical (check sail) will also be required.

**No Sailing Card:** You may challenge the sailing qualifications, by taking a written exam and passing a full practical check sail. Appointment for check sails may be necessary and there is a fee for practical check sails.

**Expos and Capri 16.5:** Skippers must have a Camp Pendleton certification card, anyone under the age of 18 must be under the direct supervision of an individual at least 18 years old. Expos and Capri 16.5 are restricted to the harbors. Sailors ages 16 and up may rent Capri.16.5. 10-17 year old skippers are limited to the boat basin only. Capri 16.5 when racing are required to have a crew member.

**22' Sailing Vessels:** Skippers must be age 18 or above. You must have a Camp Pendleton certification card. There is a maximum of 5 persons on board the 22s.

**25' and 27' Sailing Vessels:** Skippers must be age 18 or above. There is a maximum of 6 persons on board. A minimum of 24 hours of actual sail time must be logged by the skipper on 22′ boats in order to initiate procedures for the rental of a 25' vessel. A minimum of 24 hours of actual sail time must be logged by the skipper on 25′ boats in order to initiate procedures for the rental of a 27′.

**30' Vessels:** Skipper must be age 18 or above. There is a maximum of 6 persons on board. A minimum of 35 hours of actual sail time must be logged by the skipper on 27′ boats in order to initiate procedures for 30′ rentals. Actual sail time aboard Del Mar Marina vessels or verified logged ocean time from other military facilities.

**Power Qualifications:** Must be a holder of a card stating they are certified in a power boat. If you don't have one, you can challenge by passing a written exam.

**Boston Whalers:** Skipper must be 18 years old or above. Skipper is fully responsible for strict adherence of all navigation rules. Skipper is responsible for cleanup of the vessel. Alcoholic beverages are prohibited. Maximum of 4 persons or a collective weight of 650 lbs is allowed. Skipper is responsible for all fishing licenses from base and state agencies. No water skiing, tow toys, and beaching is not allowed.

**Duffy:** Skipper must be 18 years old or above. Skipper must pass a practical check out prior to renting the vessel. Skipper is responsible for clean-up of the vessel. Alcoholic beverages are prohibited. There will be no beaching of the vessel. No fishing or swimming from this vessel. There is a maximum of 9 people with a collective weight of 1500 lbs allowed on this vessel. Life jackets must be worn by all non-swimmers and children under the age of 13.

**Towing:** In accepting outside commercial assistance, renters can incur large personal liens. Vessel Assist, Sea Tow, etc., charge renters for towing and renters are responsible for those costs. If you need assistance call the Marina staff on VHF 68 or contact at (760) 725-2820.

**Boat Return Time:** All vessels must be tied up at docks at 5pm DST (March - November) and 4pm PST (November - February).

**Late Return Charge:** $25 for every 15 minutes past the required return time. Example: 1-15 min late is $25, 16-30min late is $50 etc.

## Marina Storage & Slip Rentals
**Wet Slips**

The marina offers 85 wet slips available for monthly rental, accommodating vessels ranging from 26-73 feet in length. A limited number of longer end-tie slips are also available. A waiting list is maintained for all slip sizes; however, active duty military personnel receive priority placement.

Monthly slip rentals include: parking, fresh water hookup service, 30-amp electrical power, access to restrooms and showers, laundry facilities, and a soft drink vending machine. Slip fees are calculated based on the vessel's overall length or the slip length, whichever is greater.

Dock boxes are available for monthly rental, providing secure onboard storage for equipment and personal gear.

**Dry Storage**

The marina offers a limited number of dry storage spaces for vessels stored on trailers. Maximum combined boat and trailer length is 30 feet.

**Kayak & Dinghy Storage**

Convenient rack storage is available for kayaks, paddlecraft, or small dinghies. Storage spaces are rented monthly and provide a secure, organized location for keeping your watercraft ready for use.

For current rates and availability, please refer to the marina's pricing information or contact the office directly.

**Other Fees**

# Marine Memorial Golf Course

Unyielding to the seasoned, yet playable for the novice, William P. Bell's Marine Memorial Golf Course has been praised for its bunkers, ingenuity, and innovations in golf course construction. Enjoy the Marine Corps heritage of this course and play for the history, the heroes, and the tradition.

[BOOK A TEE TIME](https://www.chronogolf.com/club/marine-memorial-golf-course-california) · [JOIN WAITLIST](https://camppendletonmarinememorial.noteefy.app/)

Open to the public. Apply for base access. There is a one-week wait for processing. Once approved, access is valid for 90 days.

- 6,865 yards from the Tip
- Chipping Areas
- 18 Hole – Par 72
- Non-Metal Spike Course
- Sand Bunkers
- Natural Grass Driving Range
- Practice Putting Green

## Lessons
- Private Lessons
- Junior Golf
- Summer Golf Camps
- Skills Challenges
- Couples Lessons

All classes are given by PGA Professionals and Apprentices. Call for rates and details: (760) 725-4653

## Tournaments
Customized packages are available with an array of catering options to meet any budget. A Tournament Representative assists in coordinating every aspect of the event.

Contact the Tournament Coordinator for more information or call (760) 763-7869.

**Tournament Fees (Mon, Tue, Fri)**
- E1-E5 (Active): $45
- E6+ (Active)/Retired Military/DoD: $55
- Civilian: $70

## Membership
Become a member of the Marine Memorial Golf Course! Score incredible savings! No longer do you have to wait for Twilight or Super Twilight rates for the best deal. Membership allows you to play when you want, any time of day (tee time required). Play six holes, play twenty holes, or play what you like…it is all included in your membership!

**Two Types of Memberships:**
- 7-days/week: Green fee; perfect for walkers.
- 5-days/week: Green fee and cart fee, Mon–Fri.

**Membership Fees**
- Retired Military: $2,000
- DoD & Veterans: $2,250
- Civilian: $2,500

**3-Month, 6-Month, 12-Month Options**

| Rank | 3 Months | 6 Months | 12 Months |
|---|---|---|---|
| E5-Below | $300 | $450 | $720 |
| E6-O3 | $450 | $730 | $1,165 |
| O4 and Above | $500 | $800 | $1,280 |

## Foot Golf
Soccer and golf come together to create fun for every age group. Play by kicking a soccer ball on the Leatherneck 9; kick the ball into an oversized hole in the fewest amount of kicks.

**Fees:** 9 Holes; Soccer Ball Rental $7, $5

Unit PT and Special Groups Available: Call (760) 763-7869/725-GOLF or visit the Pro Shop for more information.

**Rules:**
- Your ball must be easy to identify.
- Kick off your ball from the position up to two ball lengths behind and in between the markers.
- The ball must be played as a single movement. You are not allowed to push the ball with the top or bottom of your foot. Your foot should be set separate from the ball, clearly behind, before each kick.
- Play the ball where it lies: You are not allowed to move the ball or remove jammed objects. EXCEPTION: You may mark the spot and lift the ball when it may obstruct the other player's kick or ball in any way.
- The player farthest from the hole is first to kick the ball.
- If ball comes to rest on a putting green, the player must drop their ball off and adjacent to the putting green, no nearer to the FootGolf hole (no penalty).
- The order of play is established based on score of the previous hole. The player with the best score will kick off first on the next hole followed by second, etc.
- Wear appropriate clothing (follow Base Dress Code). No soccer cleats (indoor soccer shoes are acceptable).
- Have fun!

## Scorecard - Descriptions of Holes - USMC Battles
- **Hole 1 – Tun Tavern:** A committee of the Continental Congress met at Tun Tavern to draft a resolution calling for two batallions of Marines able to fight for independence at sea and on shore. The resolution was approved on Novemver 10, 1775, officially forming the Continental Marines.
- **Hole 2 – Tripoli:** The First Barbary War (1801-1805), was the first of two Barbary Wars, in which the United States and Sweden fought against the four Barbary States. The cause of the U.S. participation was due to pirates from the Barbary States seizing American merchant ships and holding the crews for ransom. The First Barbary War showed that America could execute a war far from home and that American forces had the cohesion to fight together as Americans, rather than separate statesmen.
- **Hole 3 – Battle of Derna:** The turning point in the First Barbary War was the Battle of Derna (April-May 1805). This was the first time the United States flag was raised in victory on foreign soil. The action was memorialized in a line of the Marines' Hymn – "the shores of Tripoli." It is fabled that Lieutenant O'Bannon performed so heroically that he was presented a sword from Pasha Hamet Karamanli. The sword later became the pattern for the swords that are carried by the Marine Corps officers today.
- **Hole 4 – Battle of Chapultepec:** The Battle of Chapultepec in September 1847 was an assault by American forces on the Mexican forces holding Chapultepec in Mexico City. The castle, sitting atop a 200-foot tall hill was an important position for the defense of the city. The efforts of this battle and subsequent occupation of Mexico City were later memorialized in the opening lines of the Marines' Hymn.
- **Hole 5 – Battle of Belleau Wood:** The Battle of Belleau Wood (1-26 June 1918) announced to the Germans that the United States armed forces had arrived in strength and were eager to fight. Though documented to be one of their bloodiest fights, the Marines fought off parts of five divisions of Germans and were often reduced to using only their bayonets and fists in hand-to-hand combat. The term "devil dog" is later given to the Marines by the Germans because of their tenacity.
- **Hole 6 – Battle of Guadalcanal:** On August 7, 1942, allied forces and the United States Marines land on Guadalcanal, Tulagi, and Florida in the southern Solomon Islands. The Japanese defenders who have occupied those lands since May 1842, were outnumbered and overwhelmed by the allies who captured Tulagi and Florida, as well as the airfield – later named "Henderson Field."
- **Hole 7 – Battle of Tarawa:** The Battle of Tarawa was fought in the Pacific Theater of World War II, November 20-23, 1943. The battle was the first time that the United States had faced serious Japanese opposition to an amphibious landing. Due to low tide, United States landing crafts would get snagged up in the coral reefs. 4,500 Japanese troops attempted to take advantage of this misfortune but they were no match for the 18,000 Americans.
- **Hole 8 – Battle of Peleliu:** The battle of Peleliu, codenamed "Operation Stalemate II" by the United States military, was fought between the United States and Japan during the Mariana and Palau Campaign of World War II, from September-November 1944, on the island of Peleliu. This battle was part of a larger offensive campaign known as Operation Forager, which ran from June-November 1944, in the Pacific Theater. The National Museum of the Marine Corps called it "the bitterest battle of the war for the Marines."
- **Hole 9 – Battle of Iwo Jima:** The Battle of Iwo Jima (February 19 - March 26, 1945) was a major battle in which the United States Marine Corps and Navy landed on and eventually captured the island of Iwo Jima from the Imperial Japanese Army during World War II. The American invasion had the goal of capturing the entire island. This five-week battle comprised some of the fiercest and bloodiest fighting of the Pacific War of World War II.
- **Hole 10 – Battle of Okinawa:** The Battle of Okinawa, codenamed "Operation Iceberg" was a major battle of the Pacific War fought on the island of Okinawa by the United States Marine and Army forces against the Imperial Japanese Army. The initial invasion of Okinawa on April 1, 1945, was the largest amphibious assault in the Pacific Theater of World War II.
- **Hole 11 – Battle of Inchon:** The Battle of Inchon (September 15, 1950) was an amphibious invasion and battle during the Korean War that resulted in a decisive victory and strategic reversal in favor of the United Nations Command. The operation involved some 75,000 troops and 261 naval vessels and led to the recapture of the South Korean capital of Seoul.
- **Hole 12 – Battle of Chosin Reservoir:** The Battle of Chosin Reservoir took place a month after the People's Republic of China entered the conflict and sent the People's Volunteer Army to infiltrate the northeastern part of North Korea. On November 27, 1950, the Chinese forces surprised the United States X Corps at the Chosin Reservoir area. A brutal 17-day battle in freezing weather soon followed.
- **Hole 13 – Operation Union:** Operation Union was a search and destroy mission in the Que Son Valley carried out by the 1st Marine Regiment from April 21 - May 16, 1967. The object of the operation was to engage the People's Army of Vietnam 2nd Division. Operation Union concluded with the 5th Marine Regiment being awarded the Presidential Unit Citation award by President Lyndon Johnson. On May 26, 5th Marines, which had assumed control of the latter stages of Operation Union, kicked off Operation Union II.
- **Hole 14 – Battle of Khe Sanh:** The Battle of Khe Sanh (January 21 - July 9, 1968) was conducted in the Khe Sanh area of northwestern Quang Tri Province, Republic of Vietnam during the Vietnam War. The main United States forces defending Khe Sanh Combat Base were two regiments of the Marine Corps supported by elements from the Army, Air Force, and Army of the Republic of Vietnam troops.
- **Hole 15 – Battle of Hue:** The Battle of Hue was one of the longest and bloodiest battles of the Vietnam War. Between January 31 and March 3, 1968, 18 battalions from the Army of the Republic of Vietnam, the Army, and the Marine Corps defeated 10 battalions of the People's Army of Vietnam and the Viet Cong.
- **Hole 16 – The Gulf War (The Battle of Khafji):** The Battle of Khafji was the first major ground engagement of the Persian Gulf War. It took place in and around the Saudi Arabian city of Khafji from January 29 - February 1, 1991 and marked the culmination of the Coalition's air campaign over Kuwait and Iraq.
- **Hole 17 – Operation Iraqi Freedom:** On March 19, 2003, an ultimatum given to the regime of Saddam Hussein expired, so the United States and an allied coalition began what was known as, "Operation Iraqi Freedom." The military objectives of Operation Iraqi Freedom consisted of ending the regime of Saddam Hussein, identifying, isolating, and eliminating Iraq's weapons of mass destruction, and searching for, capturing, and driving out terrorists from the country.
- **Hole 18 – Battle of Ramadi:** The Battle of Ramadi was fought during the Iraq War from March - November 2006 in order to gain control of the capital of the Al Anbar Governorate in western Iraq. A combined force of Marines, Navy, and Iraqi Security Forces fought insurgents for control of key locations in Ramadi. Intense fighting in the later months of the battle largely eliminated al-Queda from the city.

pages.text:
# Outdoor Adventures

Outdoor Adventures is a program that exposes active duty service members to outdoor recreational activities.

*Active duty only.*

All events are one-day activities located on the base or within 120 miles of the surrounding base areas. Equipment is provided during events and scheduled activities. Equipment is not available for individual rental or checkout.

## Unit Recreation
Outdoor Adventures unit-based recreation is a free program for all active duty units aboard Camp Pendleton. Units must request an event at least two weeks in advance, and no more than four months in advance of the desired date. Activities offered vary based on weather, event location, and unit size.

Possible activities include surfing, stand-up paddle boarding, snorkeling, archery, mountain biking, and hiking. Units may select other activities but would be responsible for associated fees.

## Active Duty Recreation
Outdoor Adventures offers active duty service members aboard Camp Pendleton recreational opportunities that are fee-based. Activities are advertised and booked first-come first-serve basis, geared towards smaller groups.

Activities may include ski and snowboard trips, beach days with surfing, stand-up paddle boarding and snorkeling, deep sea fishing, archery, mountain biking, and hiking.

## Alternative Workouts
Free unit events featuring:

- Surf lessons
- Stand-up Paddle Boarding
- Hiking
- Mountain Biking
- Archery

[Schedule a free alternative PT activity](mailto:pen.oa@usmc-mccs.org) for your unit.

*Active duty only.*

# Recreation Checkout

Get your propane refilled at Recreation Checkout for $3.83/gallon!

## Inflatable Rentals
**Availability**
Inflatables can be reserved on a first come first serve basis. Please don't hesitate!
Monday - Friday, we rent 5 inflatables per day.
Saturday - Sunday, we rent 10 inflatables per day.

**Loading, Transporting, and Unloading**
Inflatables are very heavy ranging from 200-400 lbs. The patron bears responsibility for loading and unloading. A full size, open bed pickup truck, and a minimum of two people capable of lifting 150 lbs. each are required for larger items.

**Return Times**
Patrons that have reserved inflatables are allowed to pick it up at 8am when the facility opens. The inflatable must be returned by 9am on the day it is due. Items returned after 9am incur an additional day fee.

**Cleaning**
Please return inflatables clean and in the same condition as when checked out, as other patrons that have reserved an inflatable are picking up the same unit you are returning. Silly string use is strictly prohibited and cannot be used in, on, or around any inflatable because it chemically bonds (like glue) to the inflatable's vinyl surface. Removal could cost hundreds of dollars.

**Inflatables Must Not Get Wet**
If the unit is to be used in an area with automatic sprinklers, please ensure the system has been shut off for at least one full day prior to and on the day of your event. Setup areas must be dry. Wait until dew has evaporated before setting up; take down and secure indoors before it settles on the unit. Units cannot be left outdoors overnight.

## RV/Vehicle/Motorcycle Storage
**Four things you need to provide:**
1. Your military ID
2. RV, boat, or trailer registration with your name as the owner
3. Credit Card to put on file; auto-debit billing is a requirement for storage
4. The RV, boat, trailer, etc. that you are storing; the equipment has to be measured to ensure it is being placed in the appropriate size space

- Storage of joint ownership property is prohibited unless all joint owners are authorized patrons.
- Your vehicle can only be stored or removed by you or someone that is your Power of Attorney.
- Vehicle registration and insurance must remain active. The vehicle must remain legally operational within the state of California while in storage. The vehicle cannot be registered as non-operational.
- We do not store unregistered or registered "project type" RVs, buses, racing, off-road; only cars, trucks, or motorcycles.
- The vehicle must be maintained while in storage. Windows cannot be broken, tires cannot be flat, body-panels and engine hoods cannot be missing.
- All vehicles are to be stored sitting on their tires - You are not allowed to put your vehicle on blocks.
- Open cargo trailers cannot be stored with anything on top of them. Nothing can be stored on top or on the outside of enclosed cargo trailers, RVs, or boats.
- Nothing can be left on the ground within the space. Items left on the ground will be picked up and treated as lost & found. If unclaimed, they will be discarded after 14 days.
- We do not take responsibility for contacting patrons regarding lost & found items.
- Only one item allowed per space.
- We do not store semi-truck trailers.
- Storage agreement paperwork will be initiated/completed only when the vehicle is stored. Due to peak storage times allow 30 mins. to store your vehicle.
- If the vehicle is going to be covered, extra tie downs are necessary to make sure it stays on. We do not take responsibility for car covers.
- Vehicle maintenance is not allowed in the storage lots.

**Additional Motorcycle Requirements**
- Motorcycle storage containers are for motorcycles only. They are not personal storage units. Storage of hazardous materials or liquids is not permitted.
- More than one motorcycle may be stored. However, only one patron will be responsible for billing. Registration and insurance must be provided for all motorcycles. Each registered owner must be a valid patron.
- D-ring tie-downs are provided. We do not take responsibility for tying down motorcycles, you must provide your own straps.
- Motorcycle maintenance is not allowed in the storage lots.

**Privately Owned Vehicle (POV) Storage Information:** POV storage is only for deployed service members.
- Storage Agreement paperwork will be initiated / completed ONLY when the vehicle is stored. Unlimited POV storage is generally available. Due to peak storage times allow 30 minutes to store your vehicle. Paperwork usually takes 5-10 minutes.
- As a customer service, facility personnel disconnect the vehicle's battery upon storage and reconnect, jump start, and air up tires as necessary upon removal.
- If the vehicle is going to be covered with a car cover, extra rope is necessary for effective protection. Please write your name & phone number on the front of the car cover. We will call if it's found in the lot. Car covers found in the lot will be stored for 3 months, then disposed of.

**Who can store my vehicle?** 1. You 2. Your spouse 3. Anyone that is designated to be your Special Power of Attorney

**Other Recommendations**
- Vehicle's fuel tank should be stored full of stabilized fuel (follow product directions). Place an opened box of fabric softener sheets or mothballs in the engine compartment to deter rodent activity.
- Close all interior vents and windows and with your hands make sure all doors, hatches, etc. are locked.

Recreation Checkout reserves the right to not store equipment that is 10 years or older. The Facility Manager or other Supervisor will determine the condition of the property to be stored and has the authority to refuse storage of unsafe, unsightly, or deteriorating property. The Facility Manager or Supervisor can also determine to store equipment that is older than 10 years based on its condition. Recreation Checkout does not store property that is considered a project or becomes a project.

## Trailer Rentals and Deployed POV Storage
Renting a teardrop travel trailer from MCCS Recreation Checkout is easy and hassle-free. Simply give us a call to make your reservation or stop by to check out the trailer and all we offer! Our friendly and knowledgeable staff will be more than happy to assist you with any questions or concerns that you may have. We offer flexible rental options to accommodate your specific needs, whether you're planning a short weekend trip or an extended vacation.

**Six Requirements:**
1. Military ID
2. Deployment Orders
3. Credit Card with your name on it
4. Vehicle Registration with your name on it
5. Current Proof of Insurance with your name on it
6. Keys to door, ignition, and any anti-theft device (alarm remote, etc.)

- Advanced payment required for 6 months (length of deployment), and a credit card on file for Auto-Debit Billing, which will only take effect if your deployment goes beyond 6 months.
- Deployment storage applies only to POV's. It does not include trailers, boats, RVs, or other items.
- Storage of joint ownership property is authorized only with immediate family members or next of kin with Power of Attorney.
- Your vehicle can only be stored or removed by you or someone that is your Power of Attorney.
- We will store one additional vehicle for dependent spouses of deployed Service Members at the same rate with all the same requirements.
- Vehicle must be currently registered, insured, and operational.
- All vehicles are to be stored sitting on their tires - You are not allowed to put your vehicle up on blocks.
- Storage agreement paperwork will be initiated / completed only when the vehicle is stored. Due to peak storage times allow 30 minutes. Paperwork usually takes 5-10 minutes.
- We will disconnect the vehicle battery upon storage.
- We will also reconnect the battery, jump start and air up tires as necessary upon removal.
- We do not periodically start or maintain the vehicle.
- If the vehicle is going to be covered with a car cover, extra tie downs are necessary to make sure it stays on. We do not take any responsibility for car covers.

## Unit Gear Rentals
Recreation Checkout has everything necessary to enhance family days or unit events, all at no cost to you: inflatable jump houses, sumo suit games, E-Z UP canopies, coolers, towable propane and charcoal barbecues (with or without electric rotisserie), and non-towable griddles.

Connect with your Deployment Readiness Coordinator or Unit Readiness Coordinator in order to reserve your equipment. All Units reach out to their assigned Deployment Readiness Coordinator (DRC). The DRC will fill out the unit gear request form and contract and will submit them to their respective M&FP Coordinator. All Unit requests are placed on reserve at that time and reservations are made 30-days out as first come, first serve. Request agreement is between Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS), Marine Corps Base (MCB), Camp Pendleton, California, and the undersigned Uniformed/Deployment Readiness Coordinator (U/DRC) for the temporary loan of the Unit Gear.

- Gear can be picked up at 11am and must be returned by 9:30am.
- If a unit returns gear late, the unit will be put on a no use restriction for a 30 day period.
- If a unit returns gear late, causing another unit to miss their reservation, the late unit will be put on a no use restriction for 60 days.
- Any replacement costs for missing parts/pieces, and/or any damaged equipment will be charged to the respective U&FRF cost center.
- Recreation Checkout will not accept any form of payment from a Service Member or U/DRC's private bank account or insurance carrier.
- Recreation Checkout will send an invoice for payment to the U/DRC prior to charging the unit cost center.
- Unit gear can only be picked up and returned Mon-Fri. Upon return, the unit's working party will be required to set-up, clean, inspect, and put away the equipment. See the unit gear request forms for further details.
- Units will not be held liable for broken or non-functioning equipment when the defect is caused by normal wear and tear.
- The DRC does not have to be present to pick up or drop off gear.
- The unit POC for pick-up and drop-off are expected to inspect the equipment along with a Recreation Checkout Staff member.
- The pick-up POC for the units will have discretion to not accept gear that is not in good condition or not functioning properly.
- The DRC is ultimately responsible for the proper and timely pick-up, return, care of, and accountability of the equipment.
- The Unit Commander and U/DRC are responsible for the safety of anyone using the equipment.
- Recreation Checkout cannot be held liable for injuries or mishaps that occur during the use of loaned gear.
- It is incumbent upon the U/DRC to ensure that Service Members utilizing their POVs for pick-up or drop off have current registration, insurance and license.
- The undersigned U/DRC, on behalf of the respective unit, agrees to accept financial responsibility for all equipment returned late, missing parts/pieces, or damaged and in need of repair.
- Other equipment is available at a cost – please refer to our current price list and coordinate with your U/DRC for specific pricing, availability, and process.

Please download the [request form](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=2ff578d5-5231-4d69-bbda-059f41a7385a&v=3) and e-mail to: reccheckoutcp@usmc-mccs.org

## General Rental Policies
- Authorized patrons include Retirees, Active Duty Service Members, 100% Disabled Veterans, DoD Personnel, and their adult dependents (18 years and older).
- Payment, in full, is due at the time of reservation. If equipment is picked up early, all advance fees are due at the time of pick-up.
- If equipment is returned late, a late fee payment, in full, is due at the time of drop off.
- Patrons are responsible for loading and unloading their equipment. Recreation Checkout does not take responsibility for damage to vehicles.
- Prices do not include cleaning (except sleeping bags). All equipment must be returned in a clean and working condition.
- Items may be reserved in person up to one month in advance (example: reserve on May 10th for June 10th) or by phone if we have served you before. Lost and found items will be held for 14 days and then discarded. Recreation Checkout does not take responsibility for contacting patrons concerning lost and found items.
- Cancellations must be made prior to 48 hours of pickup. Cancellations made within 48 hours of pickup will be subject to a fee of 25% of the total cost.

**Trailer Rentals:** In addition to general rental policies. Insurance, military ID, and driver's license for the driver of the tow vehicle must be current. The tow vehicle must be equipped with a 2" ball hitch and flat 4-prong light connector. We reserve the right to not hook up a trailer to any hitch that is not correctly rated or appears to be unsafe. If you are uncertain, please ask one of our staff members to inspect your hitch prior to reserving your trailer.

**Inflatable Jumper Rentals:** In addition to the general rental policies, it is the patron's responsibility to safely load, unload, and transport a 200-600lb jumper. We reserve the right to not allow a jumper to be loaded if an unsafe condition exists. SILLY STRING IS STRICTLY PROHIBITED. It adheres to the surface of the jumper and in some cases can render the jumper damaged beyond repair. If you return a jumper with silly string residue, you could be liable for the replacement cost of the jumper or pay a cleaning fee. Do not allow jumpers to get wet. Wet jumpers require two days of drying time. If you return a jumper wet, you will be charged an additional two days of rental fees. Does not apply to wet slides. If your jumper is returned excessively dirty, you will be contacted to pay a cleaning fee of one additional rental day.

# Recreational Shooting

**NOTICE:** Range 216 Recreational Shooting will permanently close after Friday, October 30, 2026.

*Please call ahead as our range schedule is subject to change based on unit training and mission requirements.*

Check us out at the Pistol and Rifle range, just south of Camp Horno. Please call ahead. Our range schedule is subject to change based on unit training and mission requirements.

Everything you need to shoot is available on site:

- Targets with stands
- **FREE** basic instructions
- Rental guns will use range ammunition **ONLY**
- Drinking water and chemical toilets are available
- Eye and ear protection can be purchased from the cashier's booth

## Range Commands and Follow-On Actions
- **"Cease Fire"** – Stop shooting.
- **"Clear Guns"** – Remove ammunition source and clear chamber.
- **"Range Cold"** – Do not handle your firearm at this time.
- **"Eyes and Ears"** – Ensure hearing and eye protection are worn.
- **"Range Hot"** – Start shooting.

Cease fire for status at the top of the hour for target placement/maintenance and to accomplish brass call.

## Range Information
- Check-in at the green container.
- **No reloads.**
- Long pants and close-toed shoes are required.
- A minimum of a T-shirt length shirt required.
- Bring hearing and eye protection.
- Parking lot is behind the Ready line.
- Please park large trucks/jeeps in grass/dirt area.
- Personal weapons are allowed.
- Military family members and guests are allowed to use the range.
- Civilian usage is allowed if you have access to the base or are a guest of a base access holder.
- Targets and stands are available onsite.
- Turn in misfire/defective munition to Range Safety Officer.
- For shotguns, no clay pigeons are allowed.
- Rental guns will use range ammunition only.
- Drinking water is available.
- Portable chemical toilets are available.

## MCX Firearm Promo
**New to shooting or purchasing a firearm?**

Get free firearms instruction with your MCX firearms purchase at Recreational Shooting, Camp Pendleton! This offer is perfect for new firearms owners looking for a safe and educational experience. Call today!

*Please call (760) 212-1973.*

*MCX sales receipt is required to book this free offer.*

## Eligibility
Our facility is open to active duty personnel/dependents, retired military/dependents, authorized DoD personnel, and civilian guests.

Pistol rentals are available, with no rifle rentals at this time.

## Personal Firearms
- **No reloads.**
- Weapon must be transported as per [California regulations](https://oag.ca.gov/firearms/travel).
- Any firearm must be carried directly to and from any lawful operation or purpose must be contained within a locked container. Ammunition must be placed in separate physical location.

**Pistol Range:** Paper targets 3-75 yards

**Rifle Range:** Paper targets 25-400 yards; Steel targets 100-1000 meters

**Pistols to Rent:** Berretta 92 FS; Springfield 1911 EMP; Ruger GP 100

**Ammunition Available for Purchase:** .22LR, .223, .308, .380 Cal, .38 Cal, .40, .45 ACP, 6.5CM, 7.62X39, X51, 9mm

pages.title: Stepp Stables
pages.text:
# Stepp Stables

## Notice
Our leadership continuously evaluates installation programs and infrastructure to ensure resources are aligned with the evolving needs of today's military families. After careful consideration, the command has decided to phase out stables operations so resources can be redirected to higher-demand recreational and community programs that serve a broader segment of the installation population.

Stepp Stables will continue normal operations through February 28, 2027.

## Current Boarding Opportunity
Stepp Stables is accepting new boarders on a month-to-month basis for self-care boarding only. This temporary boarding opportunity will be available through February 1, 2027.

## Policy
- Please go directly to the office (BLDG 15016) upon arrival.
- Do not pet/feed horses without the owner's permission.
- Long pants and close-toed shoes are required at all times while on Stepp Stables property.
- Helmets are required for everyone under 18 years of age. If jumping, helmets are always required, no exceptions. Riding gloves are encouraged but not required.
- A caretaker form must be filled out for anyone taking care/riding another patron's horse. This will need to be approved by the manager prior to care/riding.
- We are always open for volunteers! Anyone under the age of 13 years is required to have a parent or guardian present on Stepp Stables property for the duration of the volunteer work.

## Eligibility and Services
Open daily to the public for boarding. Stepp Stables services military, DoD employees, and civilians.

Stepp Stables is open to active-duty military personnel, Department of War (DoW) employees, and authorized civilian patrons. We provide exceptional customer service and offer a range of premium boarding options, including full-service, self-service, and lot pasture to accommodate a variety of needs and lifestyles.

**Civilian Sponsorship and Base Access**

Civilians are able to board with us even if they do not have regular base access. Please email us for more information. We will need a copy of a REAL ID for sponsorship onto the base. Once you have signed a contract with us, we provide a DBIDS pass which is good for one year and will need to be renewed annually by stables management. Please message stables management once you're within one (1) month prior to the expiration date of your DBIDS.

The DBIDS offers 24/7 access through the San Luis Rey Gate only. Please refer to the attached link for additional instructions on obtaining base access. At this time, each boarding contract may sponsor up to two individuals for a DBIDS.

All lessons and trail rides are limited availability and by appointment only. Forms can be found at Light Speed which can be filled out in advance and brought in the day of your scheduled appointment. We offer riding lessons to ages 3+ and trail rides to ages 7+. Give us a call today to schedule!

## Facilities
- three arenas (dragged/watered around 4 times a week)
  - upper arena: 96x185 (17,760 sq ft)
  - middle arena: 100x250 (25,000 sq ft)
  - lower arena: 100x230 (23,000 sq ft)
- three round pens
- three wash racks
- miles of scenic trail riding
- turnout pens
- over 100 24' x 24' mare motel stalls
- individual tack rooms (included with stall)
- automatic waterers
- alfalfa and Bermuda available at facility
- sand available at facility for purchase
- trailer parking (additional fee)
- fly trap services

## Pricing
**Feed Fees**

| Service | Military | Civilian |
|---|---|---|
| Full Feed | $525 | $625 |
| Self Service* | $350 | $475 |
| Lot Pasture | $350 | $400 |

*Interested in Self Service but unable to visit twice daily? Ask us about our Caretaker Form! This option allows you to designate another authorized boarder or a patron with existing base access to provide care for your horse. The Caretaker Form must be completed in advance and is subject to approval by the Stepp Stables manager.

**Service Fees**
- Trailer Parking (assigned parking spot): $40/month

**Emergency Veterinary Care Fees:** Fees are varied and based on care and treatment.

## Feeding Options
**Full Service**
Includes one 24' x 24' mare motel-style stall, one assigned tack room, and one automatic waterer. Stepp Stables provides twice a day feedings which includes hay (Alfalfa and/or Bermuda), 2 flakes am/pm as well as once a day stall cleaning. Stables will provide a minimum of once daily fecal output checks as well as water bucket checks/fillings. Boarder to pay additional for sand, which can be dumped/spread by stables staff for an additional charge, or can provide own shavings as well. Owners are responsible for veterinarian/farrier appointments. Please forward all required medical records to management.

**Self Service**
Includes one 24' x 24' mare motel-style stall, one assigned tack room, and one automatic waterer. Alfalfa and Bermuda hay is available for purchase and includes free delivery to assigned tack room. Boarder to pay additional for sand, which can be dumped/spread by stables staff for an additional charge, or can provide own shavings as well. Owners are responsible for veterinarian/farrier appointments. Please forward all required medical records to management.

**Lot Pasture**
Includes two flakes of Alfalfa twice a day, one shared automatic waterer tub checked daily, and paddock dragging/cleaning on an as-needed basis. Both mares and geldings share the lot pasture area and are slowly integrated with each other. Owners are responsible for veterinarian/farrier appointments. Please forward all required medical records to management.

**MCCS Herd Pasture**
This private space is available under a single contract (military or civilian) and offers access to all facility amenities and includes five, 24x24' mare-motel style stalls, hay feeders, a private small pasture, water trough, and shade area. Plus three large arenas, three wash racks, three round pens, miles of scenic riding trails, and ample trailer parking.

If you are interested in scheduling a tour or would like more information, please contact us at pendletonsteppstables@usmc-mccs.org.

**Boarding Requirements:** Please [view Boarding Requirements document](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=76f8e590-dcc1-4a59-8a80-712e308e62b3&v=3).

## Lesson / Trail Contractors
_COMING SOON_

Interested in giving lessons? Maybe trails are more your thing?

Stepp Stables will be hiring contractors to provide these services. You provide the horse/equipment, we provide the facility.

Requirements and more coming soon. Please reach out to us via email and we'll provide more information and updates on when the program is up and running.

## Stepp Stables Rules & Regulations
Please [view Rules & Regulations document](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=9c5a003d-ce0e-433c-9ab2-366b4af45d0f&v=1).

**Animal Care**
Ensure that your horse has proper medical care, hoof care, feed, and exercise. Owner must ensure that the horse receives proper care as approved by the MCCS Stepp Stables Manager as outlined in the boarding agreement. Horses may be placed on full feed or full cleaning without owner permission at the discretion of Stables management and may be reported to Animal Control. Animal abuse will not be tolerated at any time. Animal abuse and/or neglect may result in border being evicted from the stables and a report submitted to the Humane Society.

**Pen Maintenance**
Pen façades must be kept neat and clean. Equipment such as muck rakes must be hung up and off the ground. Halters and lead ropes may be hung from wall hooks. All other equipment must be stored in tack sheds. Stables staff at management's discretion will remove all items not stored in the tack rooms. Please keep all stall gates closed and latched at all times. If gates are opened, please open to the inside.

**Common Area Cleanliness**
Clean up after yourselves, your horses, and dogs in common areas. Clean up any trash or mess that you create. This includes hay outside tack sheds and stalls, waste from grooming and clipping, and all manure, equine and canine. Owners are responsible at all times for controlling the behavior of their pets. No dog shall be allowed to roam free at any time. Dogs must be on a leash at all times.

**Stall Cleaning**
Stalls must be cleaned a minimum of four times per week. Water troughs, buckets, automatic waters, etc. must be cleaned at least once weekly. Frequent stall cleaning reduces the number of flies in boarding areas. Stalls that have not been cleaned in four days will be cleaned by Stables Staff. Cleaning fees shall be assessed as outlined in the Stepp Stables Boarding Agreement.

**Manure Disposal**
Manure should be disposed of inside manure pits. Manure carts shall be empty after use. Manure shall be placed as far back as possible in the pit. Manure carts shall be returned alongside their correlating manure pit. Leaving manure carts in front of pits blocks other boarders from dumping manure. Do not dump manure in aisle ways, if a pit is full dump manure in the next closest pit.

**Arena and Turnout Usage**
Turnouts must not exceed 15 minutes regardless of the number of horses being turned out together. Lessons and riders always have priority over lunging and turnouts with no time limit. Be courteous to other boarders. One should not have to be asked to take their horse(s) out of a turnout. The practice of "I didn't see anyone waiting," is not acceptable. All turnouts must be supervised. Owners may not put their horses in an arena and leave the area or facility. Horses shall not be left unattended at any time while in the arenas, round pens, wash rack areas, on the hot walker, or at the tie rails. Horses are not to be tied to fences, shrubs, cars, tack rooms or led by an owner operating a vehicle. Use the designated hitching rails.

**Speed Limits**
The speed limit is 5mph throughout the stables. Speed limits will be kept traffic slow in common areas and adhered to whether in a vehicle or on horseback. Drive vehicles no greater than 5 mph and keep horses at a walk in the Stables areas unless in an arena, round pen, or trail course. While on trails please keep horses at a walk when passing other riders. Avoid military training while riding in training areas. Do not approach uniformed personnel, vehicles, or tents.

**Rule Violations**
Violations of these conditions may constitute grounds for loss of stable privileges.

_Stepp Stables rules and guidelines are subject to change at any time, with or without notice at the discretion of the Stables management and Food, Hospitality, and Recreation leadership._

## Trail Riding
Stepp Stables provides boarders with access to extensive scenic riding trails. Many of these historic trails, some originating as far back as the 1940s, remain visible and in use today.

[Trail maps](https://pendleton.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=inline&id=2b9fa005-8bbe-4b31-ba36-21eebc6fe58a&v=2), including distance and route details, are available at the office at no additional cost.

_For safety, all riders under 18 years of age are required to wear a helmet._

## Volunteers & LOA
Stepp Stables welcomes volunteers to support the ongoing care and maintenance of our facility. Upon request, Letter of Appreciations are available for our military volunteers in recognition of their service and contributions. Below are some of the typical tasks assigned to volunteers:

- weed whacking
- painting
- stall cleaning
- stall leveling
- pavement blowing
- power washing
- sweeping
- hay barn cleaning

Volunteers are welcome at any time during Stepp Stables' regular operating hours. Upon arrival, please check in at the Office (BLDG 15016) to complete the required volunteer forms. Volunteers are responsible for recording their hours by signing in at the beginning of their shift and signing out upon completion.

_For safety, children under 13 years of age must be accompanied by a parent or guardian at all times while at the facility._

## Fire Season
**Notice**
Dry landscaping, warmer temperatures, and Santa Ana winds may provoke fires. Causes include lightning, vehicles/machinery, ordnance, arson, cigarettes, electrical malfunction, and loss of control with controlled burns.

Boarders will be contacted by phone in the event of an emergency, and further instructions will be provided.

**Emergency Contacts**
If you see fire or smoke, call Base Fire Dispatch at 760-725-4321.
For extreme emergencies, call the Fire Emergency Line at 760-725-3333.

**Stable Safety Features & Horse Care During Fires**
Stalls are constructed of pipe corrals with metal roofs and dirt floors, surrounded by wide dirt aisleways that act as fire breaks. In the event of a fire, it may be safest to leave your horse in its stall. Ensure each horse has a halter and lead rope labeled with your name and phone number to assist emergency personnel during evacuations.

**Water & Access Limitations**
Water service may be interrupted during fire emergencies, so keep a full water bucket in your stall. When fires encroach on the area, access to Stepp Stables may be limited or denied; if access is allowed, keep your visit brief and exit quickly.

**Prohibited Activities**
Smoking or cooking near stalls or tack rooms is strictly prohibited due to the presence of hay and other flammable materials. Use the designated smoking areas listed at the facility.

**Emergency Coordination**
During major fire events, coordination is managed by the Camp Pendleton Fire Marshal and Stepp Stables management. If you are not directly involved in response efforts, please minimize your presence at the facility.

**Additional Information**
For questions or concerns, speak with Stepp Stables management or review the fire safety binder located in BLDG 15016.

*At this time, smoking is only permitted in the parking lot.

## FAQs
**I don't live on or have base access, can I still come for boarding?**
Yes, Stepp Stables is able to sponsor a DBIDS pass which will need to be renewed annually. This pass provides 24/7 access through the San Luis Rey Gate only. A valid REAL ID is required prior to entering the installation. Please reach out to Stepp Stables at pendletonsteppstables@usmc-mccs.org to set up a date to visit the facility. Each boarding contract (one per horse) may sponsor up to two individuals for a DBIDS access pass.

**What type of bedding do you offer for the stalls?**
Currently, we offer washed plaster sand. This type of sand is ideal to help reduce wildfire risks, provides a soft/cushy bedding for the horses, and keeps dust low. The sand is available for an additional cost and can be spread by staff upon request.

**How many stalls do you have? How about pasture board?**
We offer more than 100 stalls for boarding and are currently in the process of expanding our pasture board area. Any maintenance issues/concerns, please see our management team so we can schedule repairs as soon as possible.

**Are your prices comparable to out in town?**
Yes! We work hard to offer some of the most competitive prices available while still providing amenities comparable to those found at off-base facilities.

**What happens if I choose self-care for boarding and am unable to take care of them for a time?**
Please give us a call to learn more about our Caretakers Program and what it includes. Caretakers must have current base access and receive manager approval. A Caretaker Agreement must be signed prior to participating in the program.

**Do you offer recommendations for veterinarian and farrier work?**
We can offer you a list of the current veterinarians and farriers that have access to the base.

**Do you offer hay and sand for stalls?**
Yes! We offer both Alfalfa and Bermuda for purchase for our self-care boarders. Two flakes of Alfalfa are provided twice a day to our lot pasture boarders, and two flakes of Alfalfa and/or Bermuda are provided twice a day to our full-care boarders. Sand can be purchased at the office and spread for an additional charge. We can provide an estimate prior to purchase.

**Can I bring my dog?**
Yes, dogs are welcome at Stepp Stables. We kindly ask that all visitors keep their dogs on a leash while on the premises and clean up after them.

**Can I board my stallion? Any restrictions for young/unhandled horses?**
Stallions are not permitted at Stepp Stables due to liability concerns. We do, however, welcome young or unhandled horses at no additional cost.

**Can I park my trailer at the facility?**
Yes! We provide horse trailer parking exclusively for our boarders for an additional monthly fee. A trailer parking form must be completed prior to being assigned a parking space.

## Stepp Stables History
**Staff Sergeant Reckless**
Staff Sergeant Reckless was a Mongolian mare and decorated veteran of the Korean War, renowned for her extraordinary service and unwavering courage. Purchased from a Korean stable boy for $250, she went on to demonstrate a valor far beyond her modest origins. During one five-day engagement, Reckless carried more than 386 rounds of ammunition, over 95 percent of the trips made without a handler. Despite her small stature, the chestnut mare came to embody the very spirit of the United States Marine Corps. She retired from active service in 1960 and passed away in 1968. Reckless was laid to rest at Stepp Stables, where a commemorative plaque at the facility's entrance honors her enduring legacy.

**Sergeant Major William F. Stepp**
Our namesake, Sergeant Major William F. Stepp, was a distinguished Korean War veteran and recipient of the Bronze Star Medal with Valor. Following his military service, he served as the Base Stables Manager from 1968 until his retirement in 1988. In recognition of his enduring contributions, the facility was formally renamed "Stepp Stables" in his honor in 2002.

Registration is handled online during the registration periods. View the season schedules for registration periods. Youth Sports has limited spots available, so all registrations will be taken on a first-come first-served basis. After the registration period has ended or a division becomes full, the Youth Sports Program will start a waiting list. It is not guaranteed that individuals on the waiting list will be assigned to a team, but will be placed if and when a spot becomes available. For more information, please call 760-725-4188.

## Eligibility
Must be a dependent of Active Duty, Retirees, Camp Pendleton MCCS (NAF) employees or honorably discharged veterans with 100% service-connected disability to be an authorized patron in accordance with Base Order 1700.17E.

## Registration Fees
$90 per child for all sports. Fee includes a few uniform essentials.

$5 discount available for each additional child registered; first child must pay full registration fee.

## Contact Information and Resources

pages.title: RV Storage
pages.text:
# RV Storage

Whether you are a service member preparing to deploy, a recreational vehicle owner, or need to store a privately owned vehicle, there are several entities across Camp Pendleton that offer vehicle storage services. Please review the information to select the best service fit for your needs.

## Pricing
• 20': $75/month
• 30': $98/month
• 40': $130/month
• 50': $140/month
• Deployed Storage: $31/month

## Four things you need to provide
• Your military ID
• RV, boat, or trailer registration with your name as the owner
• Credit Card to put on file; auto-debit billing is a requirement for storage
• The RV, boat, trailer, etc. that you are storing; the equipment has to be measured to ensure it is being placed in the appropriate size space

## What you need to know
• Storage of joint ownership property is prohibited unless all joint owners are authorized patrons.
• Your vehicle can only be stored or removed by you or someone that is your Power of Attorney.
• Vehicle registration and insurance must remain active. The vehicle must remain legally operational within the state of California while in storage. The vehicle cannot be registered as non-operational.
• We do not store unregistered or registered "project type" RVs, buses, racing, off-road; only cars, trucks, or motorcycles.
• The vehicle must be maintained while in storage. Windows cannot be broken, tires cannot be flat, body-panels and engine hoods cannot be missing.
• All vehicles are to be stored sitting on their tires – You are not allowed to put your vehicle on blocks.
• Open cargo trailers cannot be stored with anything on top of them.
• Nothing can be stored on top or on the outside of enclosed cargo trailers, RVs, or boats. Nothing can be left on the ground within the space. Items left on the ground will be picked up and treated as lost & found. If unclaimed, they will be discarded after 14 days.
• We do not take responsibility for contacting patrons regarding lost & found items.
• Only one item allowed per space.
• We do not store semi-truck trailers.
• Storage agreement paperwork will be initiated/completed only when the vehicle is stored. Due to peak storage times allow 30 mins. to store your vehicle.
• If the vehicle is going to be covered, extra tie downs are necessary to make sure it stays on. We do not take responsibility for car covers.
• Vehicle maintenance is not allowed in the storage lots.

# Marine Corps Exchange - Pendleton

## Pacific Views MCX
The Pacific Views Marine Corps Exchange (MCX) is 147,000 Sq Ft of one-stop shopping. It is the largest exchange in the Marine Corps and is located at the Main Gate across from Pacific Plaza and the Commissary.

The largest Exchange in the MCX system offers a wide variety of merchandise: Women and Men Apparel, Young Adult Clothing, Kids and Baby Clothing, Infant and Baby Merchandise and Accessories, Shoes for the Family, Home Small Appliances, Kitchen & Dining, Household Essentials Items, Patio & Garden, Toys, Electronics including Apple Products, Video Games, Movies, Music & Books, Sports & Outdoors, Beauty, Personal Care, Health, Pets, Luggage, School & Office Supplies, Party Supplies, Cards and gift wrap, Beer, Wine, Grocery Items and Seasonal Good.

## Super Star Student
The Super Star Student Program is open to students (authorized patrons) in grades K-12, whether enrolled in a traditional classroom or home-schooled. Eligible students will receive one scratch-off card with a guaranteed prize, issued as a Super Star Student Gift Card with the value indicated on the card.

To participate, students should visit their MCX within 30 days of receiving their report card. Upon verification that the student meets the eligibility criteria, they will be given one scratch-off card with a guaranteed prize. Each student is eligible to win one MCX gift card, valued at $5, $10, $25, $50, $100, or $250.

Students who earn a B, S, or 3 average or higher during a grading period are eligible for the program. In California, the program follows the California Common Core State Standards: "Qualifying students who achieve a 2.0 average or higher in the first or second trimester, or a 3.0 average or higher in the third trimester, qualify as Super Star Students."

**Program Exclusions**

• Scratch-off cards are non-transferable and cannot be shared between individuals.
• Once a store has distributed all of their scratch-off cards for a given period (e.g., September this year through August the following year), additional cards will not be available until the next "Back to School" campaign.

Thank you all for your support and goodwill in helping our Super Star Student program continue to grow, succeed, and be a true benefit to our students!

## Ship To Store
The Navy & Marine Corps shopping benefit just got bigger! Shop online at myMCX.com and have your order shipped to your nearest participating MCX in just 3-5 days stateside or 7-10 days abroad!

All Ship to Store orders for Camp Pendleton, CA come with FREE shipping and are eligible for pick up at three locations: Pacific Views MCX, San Onofre Marine Mart, or Mainside Marine Mart.

Families of authorized shoppers are welcome to experience all that the MCX offers with discounted prices and tax-free shopping. Authorized patrons must be present.

## Recreational Shooting MCX Firearm Promo
New to shooting or purchasing a firearm?

Get free safety and instruction with your MCX firearms purchase at Recreational Shooting, Camp Pendleton! This offer is perfect for new firearms owners looking for a safe and educational experience. Call today and book space at the range!

MCX Sales receipt is required to book this free offer, please call (760) 212-1973.

## San Onofre Marine Mart
The San Onofre Marine Mart offers electronics, housewares, small kitchen appliances, family apparel, military-procured gear, snacks, milk, bread, frozen entrees, beverages, and more!

## Mainside Marine Mart
The Mainside Marine Mart offers electronics, housewares, small kitchen appliances, military-procured gear, snacks, milk, bread, frozen entrees, beverages, and more!

pages.text:
# Tree Lighting Celebration

Join MCCS and MCX Camp Pendleton as we light our 50-foot holiday tree with over 30,000 twinkling lights!

## Flip the Switch
**Date:** Saturday, November 21, 2026
**Time:** 12:00 AM - 11:59 PM
**Capacity:** Unlimited
**Address:** [Pacific Views MCX BLDG 2010 Camp Pendleton, CA](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=33.2275779,-117.3910898)

We're looking for one special military family to flip the switch on Saturday, November 21 at the Tree Lighting Celebration!

Register your family for an opportunity to light the holiday tree at the 2026 MCX Tree Lighting Celebration on Saturday, November 21. The last day to enter is **Tuesday, November 10, 2026 at midnight**. The winner will be notified via email/phone on **Monday, November 16 and must respond within 48 hours or another family will be selected.**

**WHAT HAPPENS IF MY FAMILY IS SELECTED?**

You and your family will join us on stage to flip the switch and light up the tree! Your family's presence is essential, so please only enter if you're planning to attend.

Must be active duty aboard Camp Pendleton to enter.

## Chance to Win
**Date:** Tuesday, October 20, 2026 - Wednesday, November 18, 2026
**Time:** 12:00 AM - 11:45 PM
**Capacity:** Unlimited
**Address:** [Pacific Views MCX BLDG 2010 Camp Pendleton, CA](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=33.2275779,-117.3910898)

Enter now through November 18 for a chance to win one of five $1,000 MCX holiday gift cards or one of eight $500 MCX holiday gift cards!

With these prepaid cards from MCCS, you can:

- find the perfect gifts
- fill up your tank at MCX fuel stations to get you home for the holidays
- treat yourself to some much-needed self-care

Don't miss out on this festive opportunity! Good luck!

_Winners will be notified by email. One entry per active duty military at Camp Pendleton._

## Tree Lighting Event
**Kick-off the holidays with Free Family Entertainment**

- Snow Sledding
- Face Painters
- Free Carnival Games & Rides
- Santa and Mrs. Claus photo booth (Bring your Camera and take your family picture 5pm-8pm)
- Kid's Elf Packs (assorted snacks) _while supplies last_
- Food and Beverage Tastings
- MCCS Information Booths
- Strolling Carolers

## Shuttle Service
Shuttle service from the Naval Hospital will run every 15 minutes to the venue.

## Sequence of Events
- 2pm - Shuttle Service Begins
- 5pm - Tree Lighting Event Begins
- 6:20pm - Base Leadership Holiday Message
- 6:30pm - Lighting of Holiday Tree
- 6:45pm - 7pm - Photos with Chesty
- 7:15pm - 7:30pm - Photos with Chesty
- 8pm - Tree Lighting Ends
- 9pm - Shuttle Service Ends

## Food Trucks
- 7 Siblings
- Dirty Dough
- Taco Land
- We Cookn

## Vendors
- Body Art Express Mobile Tattoo
- Butter Baked
- Caked
- Confection Perfection
- Nom Stop

## FAQs
**Who is qualified for a chance to win during the event?**
All active duty, retired, and reserve military personnel, and their dependent family members over 18 years old. _Identification required._

**Where do I go if I lose my child?**
Please educate your children to go to the customer service booth if they get lost.

**Is handicapped parking available?**
Yes, limited spots will be available. Traffic guards will direct handicapped patrons with the appropriate placards to parking areas at the Pacific Views MCX parking lot.

**Can I bring outside food or drink?**
Yes. Food and beverages will be available for purchase inside the venue and MCX. Children will receive Elf packs with assorted snacks.

**Can I bring my pets?**
Only service dogs are permitted.

**Where is the parking for the event?**
Parking for the event is located at the Naval Hospital. Trams will be available from 2pm-9pm to take you to and from the event.

**Can I bring a shopping cart into the venue area?**
Shopping carts are not allowed in the venue area. However, they are available for shopping inside the Pacific Views MCX.

**Is there a designated smoking area?**
Smoking is not permitted inside the barricaded venue area.

**Will there be restrooms available?**
Venue restrooms will be available at the east end of the Pacific Views MCX Parking Lot.

**What family activities are available?**
- Santa & Mrs. Claus – Bring your camera and take your picture from 5pm-8pm!
- Play in the snow!
- Free Carnival Games
- Face Painter
- Strolling Carolers
- Elf packs with assorted snacks for kids

**What are the hours of the event?**
The event will be held from 5pm-8pm. The Tree Lighting Ceremony will occur at approximately 6:30pm.

5pm-8pm. Please arrive early for the best available parking. Overflow parking will be available at Naval Hospital Camp Pendleton.

Trams will be available from 2pm-9pm to take you to and from the event.

**How often will the shuttle run for the parking areas?**
Shuttle will be available every 15 minutes from 2pm-9pm to take you to and from the event. Shuttle pick-up and drop-off locations will be the North Parking Lot at the Naval Hospital and the Pacific Views MCX Parking Lot.
